Small: 400 g is 4 lots of 100 g, so £2.60 ÷ 4 = £0.65, i.e. 65p per 100 g.
Large: 750 g is 7.5 lots of 100 g, so £4.50 ÷ 7.5 = £0.60, i.e. 60p per 100 g.
Lower price per 100 g is better value: 60p is less than 65p.
Answer: Large box (60p per 100 g vs 65p per 100 g)

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] At a concert, 2/5 of the audience are adults and the rest are children.
The ratio of men to women among the adults is 3 : 1.
There are 18 women. How many people are in the audience?
questions.tip: Work out the number of adults first, then use the fraction 2/5 to get back to the whole audience.
steps: Start from what you know, the women. Men : women = 3 : 1, so women are 1 part of 4.
Adults are 2/5 of the audience, so 2/5 of total = 72.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The ratio of Ella's age to Finn's age is 2 : 3.
In 5 years' time the ratio of their ages will be 3 : 4.
Work out Ella's age now.
questions.tip: Add the 5 years to both ages. Cross-multiply the ratio to form a linear equation.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] x : y = 7 : 2. Which of these is true?
questions.tip: Cross-multiply carefully: x : y = 7 : 2 means 2x = 7y, not 7x = 2y.
steps: Write the ratio as a fraction: x : y = 7 : 2 means x/y = 7/2.
Check with numbers: x = 7, y = 2 gives 2 × 7 = 14 and 7 × 2 = 14. True.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Lilac paint is made by mixing white paint and blue paint in the ratio 3 : 2 by volume.
White paint costs £6 per litre and blue paint costs £11 per litre.
Work out the cost of making 20 litres of lilac paint.
ms: M1 for 20 ÷ 5 = 4, giving 12 litres white or 8 litres blue
questions.tip: Split the 20 litres in the ratio before multiplying by the prices.
steps: Ratio 3 : 2 has 3 + 2 = 5 parts, so 1 part = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 litres.
Cost of white = 12 × £6 = £72. Cost of blue = 8 × £11 = £88.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] y is directly proportional to x. When x = 4, y = 12. Find y when x = 7.
questions.tip: Find k first. Do not just add 3 to 12 because x went up by 3.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] 6 workers take 15 days to build a wall. How long would 9 workers take, working at the same rate?
questions.tip: More workers means fewer days: this is inverse proportion, so do not scale up.
steps: More workers means fewer days, so this is inverse proportion. Find the total work first.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y is directly proportional to the square of x. When x = 5, y = 50.
Find the value of y when x = 8.
ms: M1 for y = kx² (allow y ∝ x² stated with k)
questions.tip: Square x before dividing to find k: 50 ÷ 5 = 10 is a common wrong k.
steps: Proportional to the square of x means y = kx².

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] F is inversely proportional to the square of d. When d = 3, F = 20.
(a) Find a formula for F in terms of d.
(b) Find the positive value of d when F = 5.
questions.tip: Inversely proportional to the square means k/d², not k/d and not kd².
steps: Inversely proportional to the square of d means F = k/d².
Find k: 20 = k/3² = k/9, so k = 20 × 9 = 180. Formula: F = 180/d².

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which equation describes y being inversely proportional to x?
ms: Inverse proportion: y = k/x. Its graph is a curve that never touches the axes.
questions.tip: y = x + 4 is linear but not proportional because it does not pass through the origin.
steps: Inverse proportion means y = k/x: as x gets bigger, y gets smaller.
Check the options: y = 4x² and y = 4x both grow as x grows, and y = x + 4 is not a proportion at all.
y = 4/x fits the form y = k/x with k = 4.

questions.q: [Calculator] y is directly proportional to x². x is increased by 20%. What is the percentage increase in y?
ms: New y = k(1.2x)² = 1.44kx², so y increases by 44%.
questions.tip: Square the multiplier (1.2² = 1.44), do not just double the percentage.
steps: Write y = kx². Increasing x by 20% means multiplying x by 1.2.
So y is multiplied by 1.44, which is a 44% increase. It is not 40% because the 1.2 gets squared.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The time, t seconds, for an object to fall a distance h metres is directly proportional to the square root of h.
When h = 25, t = 2.
(a) Find a formula for t in terms of h.
(b) Find h when t = 3.
questions.tip: Once you have √h, remember to square it to get h.
steps: Proportional to the square root of h means t = k√h.
Find k: 2 = k × √25 = 5k, so k = 2 ÷ 5 = 0.4. Formula: t = 0.4√h.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] a is directly proportional to b². b is inversely proportional to c.
When b = 2, a = 8. When c = 1, b = 6.
Find the value of a when c = 4.
ms: M1 for a = kb² with k = 2, i.e. a = 2b²
M1 for b = m/c with m = 6, i.e. b = 6/c
questions.tip: Use two separate constants of proportionality. Find b from c first, then a from b.
steps: There are two links, so find each formula separately. First: a = kb². 8 = k × 2² = 4k, so k = 2, giving a = 2b².
Second: b = m/c. 6 = m/1, so m = 6, giving b = 6/c.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A car travels 150 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. What is its average speed?
questions.tip: 2 hours 30 minutes is 2.5 hours, not 2.3 hours (which gives 65.2).
steps: Speed = distance ÷ time, with time in hours.
30 minutes is half an hour, so 2 hours 30 minutes = 2.5 hours (not 2.3).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Aluminium has a density of 2.7 g/cm³. A block has mass 540 g. What is its volume?
questions.tip: Use the formula triangle: V = M ÷ D. Multiplying gives 1458, which is the wrong way round.
steps: Density = mass ÷ volume, so rearrange: volume = mass ÷ density.

questions.q: [Calculator] A box exerts a force of 600 N on an area of 1.5 m². What pressure does it exert?
questions.tip: Pressure = F/A. Larger area means smaller pressure.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A cyclist travels at 15 m/s. Change this speed to km/h.
questions.tip: Multiply by 3600 to go from per second to per hour, then divide by 1000 for km.
steps: 15 m/s means 15 metres every second. There are 3600 seconds in an hour.
Change to km: 54 000 ÷ 1000 = 54 km, so 54 km/h.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Priya drives 90 km at an average speed of 60 km/h. She then drives a further 40 km at an average speed of 80 km/h.
Work out her average speed for the whole journey.
questions.tip: Average speed is total distance ÷ total time. Averaging 60 and 80 to get 70 scores zero.
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. You cannot just average 60 and 80, because she spends different times at each speed.
Time for part 1 = 90 ÷ 60 = 1.5 h. Time for part 2 = 40 ÷ 80 = 0.5 h.
Total time = 1.5 + 0.5 = 2 h. Total distance = 90 + 40 = 130 km.

questions.q:
[Calculator] An alloy is made by melting together 20 cm³ of metal A and 30 cm³ of metal B.
Metal A has density 8 g/cm³. Metal B has density 3 g/cm³.
Work out the density of the alloy. (Assume the volume does not change.)
questions.tip: Work out total mass and total volume. Do not average the two densities (5.5 is wrong).
steps: Density of the alloy = total mass ÷ total volume. Find each mass using mass = density × volume.
Metal A: 20 × 8 = 160 g. Metal B: 30 × 3 = 90 g.
Total mass = 160 + 90 = 250 g. Total volume = 20 + 30 = 50 cm³.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A solid cuboid measures 2 m by 0.5 m by 0.4 m.
When it rests on its smallest face, it exerts a pressure of 1500 N/m² on the ground.
Work out the pressure when it rests on its largest face.
ms: M1 for smallest face area 0.5 × 0.4 = 0.2 m²
M1 for largest face area 2 × 0.5 = 1 m² and 300 ÷ 1
questions.tip: The force (weight) stays the same whichever face it rests on. Only the area changes.
steps: The force (weight) is the same whichever face it rests on. Find the force using force = pressure × area.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A water tank holds 1.2 m³ of water when full. Water flows into the empty tank at 15 litres per minute.
1 m³ = 1000 litres.
How long does it take to fill the tank? Give your answer in hours and minutes.
questions.tip: 80 minutes is not 1 hour 80 minutes or 1.8 hours. Convert carefully.
steps: Change m³ to litres so the units match the flow rate: 1.2 × 1000 = 1200 litres.

questions.q: [Calculator] £5000 is invested at 3% compound interest per year. Which calculation gives the value after 4 years?
ms: Compound interest uses the multiplier 1.03 raised to the number of years.
questions.tip: 5000 + 5000 × 0.03 × 4 is simple interest.
steps: Compound interest adds 3% to the new total each year, so multiply by 1 + 0.03 = 1.03 every year.
5000 × 0.03 × 4 is simple interest, and 1.3 would be 30%, so those are wrong.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A car is bought for £18 000. Its value depreciates by 15% each year.
Work out the value of the car after 3 years.
questions.tip: Do not subtract 45%. Depreciation compounds, so use 0.85³.
steps: Losing 15% leaves 100 - 15 = 85%, so the multiplier is 0.85 each year.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Sam invests £2000 at 4.5% compound interest per year.
What is the least number of whole years before the investment is worth more than £2500?
ms: M1 for 2000 × 1.045ⁿ with at least one trial, e.g. 2000 × 1.045⁵ = 2492.36
M1 for 2000 × 1.045⁶ = 2604.52 (or both 5 and 6 values compared with 2500)
questions.tip: Show the values for both years either side of 2500 so the examiner can see your decision.
steps: The multiplier for 4.5% growth is 1.045. Try different numbers of years.
5 years: 2000 × 1.045⁵ = 2492.36, which is not more than £2500.

questions.q: [Calculator] After an 8% increase, the price of a laptop is £1404. What was the price before the increase?
questions.tip: Do not take 8% off £1404 (that gives £1291.68). Divide by the multiplier.
steps: The new price is 108% of the old one, so old price × 1.08 = 1404. Do not take 8% off £1404, as the 8% was of the old price.

questions.q: [Calculator] A colony has 8000 bacteria. The number increases by 12% each hour. How many bacteria are there after 5 hours, to 3 significant figures?
questions.tip: 12 800 is simple growth (12% × 5 = 60%). Growth compounds.
steps: 12% growth each hour means multiply by 1.12 every hour.

questions.q:
[Calculator] An investment grows from £2000 to £2420 in 2 years at a fixed rate of compound interest.
Work out the annual rate of interest.
questions.tip: Find the overall multiplier first, then take the square root because there are 2 years. 10.5% (21% ÷ 2) is wrong.
steps: Let the yearly multiplier be m. After 2 years: 2000 × m² = 2420.
A multiplier of 1.1 means a 10% increase each year.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The value of a house was £40 000 in 1990.
The value increased by 5% per year for 2 years, then decreased by 3% per year for the next 3 years.
Work out the value of the house at the end of the 5 years. Give your answer to the nearest pound.
questions.tip: Apply each multiplier the correct number of times. Do not combine as a 2% change per year.
steps: Use one multiplier for each year. Increase of 5% is × 1.05, decrease of 3% is × 0.97.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A machine loses 20% of its value each year. After 3 years it is worth £2560.
Work out its value when it was new.
questions.tip: Work backwards by dividing by the multiplier. Adding 60% to £2560 is wrong.
steps: Losing 20% each year means multiplying by 0.8 each year, so 3 years is × 0.8³ = 0.512.
Value new × 0.512 = 2560, so work backwards by dividing.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 20°. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.tip: 160° is the interior angle, not the number of sides.
steps: Exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°.
Each one is 20°, so number of sides = 360 ÷ 20 = 18.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the sum of the interior angles of a decagon (10 sides)?
questions.tip: Use (n - 2) × 180, not n × 180. 144° is one interior angle of a regular decagon.
steps: Sum of interior angles = (n - 2) × 180°, because the shape splits into n - 2 triangles.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The interior angle of a regular polygon is 150°.
Work out the number of sides of the polygon.
questions.tip: Convert to the exterior angle first, because exterior angles always add to 360°.
steps: Use exterior angles, as they add to 360°. Interior + exterior = 180°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Lines AB and CD are parallel. A straight line EF crosses AB at P and CD at Q, with E above AB and F below CD. B and D are on the same side of EF.
Angle EPB = 68°. Work out the size of angle PQD. Give a reason for each stage of your working.
ms: B1 for a correct reason: corresponding angles are equal
B1 for a fully correct chain of reasons (e.g. angle APQ = 68° as vertically opposite angles are equal, then angle PQD = 68° as alternate angles are equal, or corresponding angles stated directly)
questions.tip: Use the proper words: 'corresponding', 'alternate', 'co-interior'. 'F angles' or 'Z angles' do not score.
steps: Angle EPB is above line AB on the B side. Angle PQD is above line CD on the D side.
They are in the same position at each crossing, so they are corresponding angles.
Corresponding angles are equal (AB and CD are parallel), so angle PQD = angle EPB = 68°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A regular pentagon and a regular hexagon share a common side AB. They are drawn on opposite sides of AB.
C is the vertex of the pentagon next to B (not A), and D is the vertex of the hexagon next to B (not A).
Work out the size of angle CBD, measured outside both shapes.
ms: M1 for interior angle of pentagon = 108° or of hexagon = 120°
questions.tip: Learn how to find interior angles: (n - 2) × 180 ÷ n.
steps: Angles around point B add up to 360°. Find each interior angle at B.
Angle CBD = 360 - 108 - 120 = 132° (angles around a point add to 360°).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle ABC has side BC extended to point D. Angle BAC = x and angle ABC = y.
Prove that angle ACD = x + y. Give reasons.
questions.answer: Angle ACB = 180 - x - y (angles in a triangle sum to 180°). Angle ACD = 180 - (180 - x - y) = x + y (angles on a straight line sum to 180°).
ms: M1 for angle ACB = 180° - x - y
M1 for angle ACD = 180° - angle ACB = x + y
A1 for both reasons stated: angles in a triangle add up to 180°, and angles on a straight line add up to 180°
questions.tip: A proof must be in terms of x and y, not numbers. Every step needs a reason.
steps: Use the triangle first. Angles in a triangle add to 180°, so angle ACB = 180 - x - y.
BCD is a straight line, so angle ACB + angle ACD = 180° (angles on a straight line).
Angle ACD = 180 - (180 - x - y) = x + y.
Answer: Angle ACB = 180 - x - y (angles in a triangle sum to 180°). Angle ACD = 180 - (180 - x - y) = x + y (angles on a straight line sum to 180°).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The interior angle of a regular polygon is 4 times the size of its exterior angle. How many sides does it have?
questions.tip: Interior + exterior = 180°. Set up e + 4e = 180.
steps: Let the exterior angle be e. Then interior = 4e.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] ABCDEF is a regular hexagon. Prove that angle ACD = 90°. Give reasons for each step.
questions.answer: Interior angle = 120°. Triangle ABC is isosceles (AB = BC), so angle BCA = (180 - 120) ÷ 2 = 30°. Angle ACD = 120 - 30 = 90°.
ms: B1 for interior angle of regular hexagon = 120° (from (6 - 2) × 180 ÷ 6 or 180 - 360/6)
M1 for angle BCA = 30° using triangle ABC isosceles because AB = BC (sides of a regular hexagon are equal)
A1 for 90° with reasons: base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, angles in a triangle add to 180°
questions.tip: Say why triangle ABC is isosceles. Without the reason the proof is incomplete.
steps: Interior angle of a regular hexagon = (6 - 2) × 180 ÷ 6 = 120°.
In triangle ABC, AB = BC (sides of a regular hexagon are equal), so it is isosceles and angle BCA = angle BAC.
Angle B = 120°, so angle BCA = (180 - 120) ÷ 2 = 30° (angles in a triangle add to 180°).
Angle BCD = 120°, and it is split into BCA and ACD, so angle ACD = 120 - 30 = 90°.
Answer: Interior angle = 120°. Triangle ABC is isosceles (AB = BC), so angle BCA = (180 - 120) ÷ 2 = 30°. Angle ACD = 120 - 30 = 90°.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Points A, B and C lie on a circle with centre O. Angle AOB = 130° (at the centre). C is on the major arc. What is angle ACB?
ms: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference, so ACB = 130 ÷ 2 = 65°.
questions.tip: Halve the angle at the centre. Do not double it.
steps: Use the circle theorem: the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. Angle ABC = 74°. What is angle ADC?
ms: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°, so ADC = 180 - 74 = 106°.
questions.tip: Opposite angles add to 180°, they are not equal.
steps: ABC and ADC are opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral.
Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] AB is a diameter of a circle and C is a point on the circumference. Angle CAB = 35°. What is angle CBA?
ms: Angle ACB = 90° (angle in a semicircle). CBA = 180 - 90 - 35 = 55°.
questions.tip: Spot the diameter: the angle opposite it at the circumference is 90°.
steps: AB is a diameter, so angle ACB = 90° (the angle in a semicircle is a right angle).
Angles in triangle ABC add to 180°: CBA = 180 - 90 - 35 = 55°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A and B are points on a circle with centre O. PA and PB are tangents to the circle from an external point P. Angle APB = 48°.
Work out the size of angle AOB. Give a reason for each stage of your working.
ms: M1 for angle OAP = angle OBP = 90°
B1 for reasons: tangent is perpendicular to the radius (at the point of contact) and angles in a quadrilateral add to 360°
questions.tip: Write the full reason 'the tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius'. Just 'tangent' does not score.
steps: A tangent meets the radius at 90°, so angle OAP = 90° and angle OBP = 90°.
OAPB is a quadrilateral, and its angles add up to 360°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B, C and D lie on a circle. AC and BD are chords that cross at X. Angle BAC = 31° and angle ABD = 47°.
(a) Find angle BDC. Give a reason.
(b) Find angle ACD. Give a reason.
ms: B1 for reason: angles in the same segment are equal (angles subtended by the same arc are equal)
B1 for reason: angles in the same segment are equal
questions.tip: Identify the chord both angles stand on. BAC and BDC both stand on chord BC.
steps: Look for angles standing on the same arc. Angles in the same segment (on the same arc) are equal.
(a) Angle BAC and angle BDC both stand on arc BC, so angle BDC = angle BAC = 31°.
(b) Angle ABD and angle ACD both stand on arc AD, so angle ACD = angle ABD = 47°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B and C lie on a circle. The straight line TAS is a tangent to the circle at A. B is on the same side of the circle as T, and C is on the same side as S.
Angle TAB = 58° and angle BAC = 70°.
Find angle ABC. Give reasons for your answer.
ms: M1 for angle CAS = 180 - 58 - 70 = 52° (angles on a straight line add to 180°)
B1 for reason: alternate segment theorem (the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment)
questions.tip: Pair the tangent-chord angle with the angle at the circumference in the opposite segment.
steps: TAS is a straight line, so angles TAB + BAC + CAS = 180°.
Alternate segment theorem: the angle between the tangent and chord AC equals the angle in the other segment, which is angle ABC.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B and C are points on a circle with centre O. Angle OAC = x and angle OBC = y, with O inside triangle ABC.
Prove that angle AOB = 2 × angle ACB. Do not quote the theorem 'angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference'.
questions.answer: OA = OC = OB (radii), so triangles OAC and OBC are isosceles: angle OCA = x, angle OCB = y, so angle ACB = x + y. Angle AOC = 180 - 2x, angle BOC = 180 - 2y. Angle AOB = 360 - (180 - 2x) - (180 - 2y) = 2x + 2y = 2(x + y) = 2 × angle ACB.
ms: M1 for angle OCA = x and angle OCB = y, with reason: OA = OC = OB (radii), so base angles of isosceles triangles are equal
M1 for angle AOC = 180 - 2x and angle BOC = 180 - 2y (angles in a triangle add to 180°)
M1 for angle AOB = 360 - (180 - 2x) - (180 - 2y) (angles around a point add to 360°)
A1 for 2x + 2y = 2(x + y) = 2 × angle ACB, with all reasons given
questions.tip: A proof must state why the triangles are isosceles (radii are equal). Missing reasons lose the final mark.
steps: Draw OC. OA, OB and OC are all radii, so they are equal, making triangles OAC and OBC isosceles.
Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, so angle OCA = x and angle OCB = y. So angle ACB = x + y.
Angles in a triangle add to 180°: angle AOC = 180 - 2x and angle BOC = 180 - 2y.
Angles around O add to 360°: angle AOB = 360 - (180 - 2x) - (180 - 2y) = 2x + 2y.

Answer: OA = OC = OB (radii), so triangles OAC and OBC are isosceles: angle OCA = x, angle OCB = y, so angle ACB = x + y. Angle AOC = 180 - 2x, angle BOC = 180 - 2y. Angle AOB = 360 - (180 - 2x) - (180 - 2y) = 2x + 2y = 2(x + y) = 2 × angle ACB.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B and C are points on a circle with centre O. C lies on the major arc AB. Angle OBA = 24°.
Work out the size of angle ACB. Give reasons for each stage of your working.
ms: M1 for angle OAB = 24° (OA = OB as radii, so triangle OAB is isosceles)
M1 for angle AOB = 180 - 24 - 24 = 132° (angles in a triangle add to 180°)
B1 for reason: the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference
questions.tip: Join to the centre and look for isosceles triangles made by two radii.
steps: OA = OB (both radii), so triangle OAB is isosceles and angle OAB = angle OBA = 24°.
Angles in a triangle add to 180°: angle AOB = 180 - 24 - 24 = 132°.
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference, so angle ACB = 132 ÷ 2 = 66°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. The line PCQ is a tangent to the circle at C, with P on the same side of C as B.
Angle ADC = 100° and angle PCB = 40°.
Work out the size of angle ACB. Give reasons for each stage of your working.
ms: B1 for reason: opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°
B1 for reason: alternate segment theorem
A1 for angle ACB = 180 - 80 - 40 = 60° (angles in a triangle add up to 180°)
questions.tip: The tangent PC and chord CB make an angle equal to angle CAB in the alternate segment.
steps: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°, so angle ABC = 180 - 100 = 80°.
Alternate segment theorem: the angle between tangent PC and chord CB equals the angle in the other segment, angle BAC. So angle BAC = 40°.
Angles in triangle ABC add to 180°: angle ACB = 180 - 80 - 40 = 60°.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A circle has centre O and radius 13 cm. A chord AB has length 24 cm. What is the perpendicular distance from O to AB?
ms: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so half chord = 12. √(13² - 12²) = 5 cm.
questions.tip: Halve the chord before using Pythagoras.
steps: The perpendicular from the centre to a chord cuts the chord in half, so half of AB = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm.
This makes a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse = radius = 13 cm and one side 12 cm.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which of these is NOT a valid condition for proving two triangles congruent?
ms: AAA shows triangles are similar, but they can be different sizes, so it does not prove congruence.
questions.tip: The valid conditions are SSS, SAS, ASA (or AAS) and RHS.
steps: Congruent means exactly the same shape AND size.
SSS, SAS and RHS all fix the lengths of sides, so they fix the size.
AAA only fixes the angles. A small and a big equilateral triangle have the same angles but are not congruent, just similar.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Triangles PQR and XYZ are similar. PQ = 9 cm corresponds to XY = 15 cm. QR = 6 cm. Find YZ.
questions.tip: Adding 6 to each side (giving 12) is wrong. Similar shapes use multiplication.
steps: Similar shapes: find the scale factor from a pair of matching sides. Scale factor = 15 ÷ 9 = 5/3.
QR matches YZ, so YZ = 6 × 5/3 = 30/3 = 10 cm.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Two similar shapes have lengths in the ratio 1 : 3. The smaller shape has area 20 cm². What is the area of the larger shape?
questions.tip: Square the length scale factor for area and cube it for volume.
steps: Length scale factor = 3. Areas go up by the square of the length scale factor.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two mathematically similar containers have surface areas of 160 cm² and 360 cm².
The volume of the smaller container is 240 cm³.
Work out the volume of the larger container.
questions.tip: Go area → length (square root) → volume (cube). Multiplying 240 by 2.25 is the common wrong answer.
steps: Go from area to length to volume. Area scale factor = 360 ÷ 160 = 2.25.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Two solid cones are mathematically similar. The smaller cone has volume 54 cm³ and height 12 cm. The larger cone has volume 250 cm³.
Work out the height of the larger cone.
questions.tip: Volume ratio must be cube-rooted to get the length scale factor.
steps: Heights are lengths, so take the cube root: ∛(125/27) = 5/3 (since 5³ = 125 and 3³ = 27).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In triangle ABC, D is a point on CA and E is a point on CB such that DE is parallel to AB.
CD = 4 cm, DA = 6 cm and DE = 5 cm.
Work out the length of AB.
ms: M1 for CA = 10 cm (or recognising triangles CDE and CAB are similar)
questions.tip: Use CA = CD + DA, not DA alone. The scale factor is 10/4, not 6/4.
steps: DE is parallel to AB, so triangles CDE and CAB are similar (same angles).
CA = CD + DA = 4 + 6 = 10 cm. It matches CD = 4 cm.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCD is a parallelogram. The diagonal AC is drawn.
Prove that triangle ABC is congruent to triangle CDA.
questions.answer: AB = CD (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal). BC = DA (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal). AC is common to both triangles. So the triangles are congruent (SSS).
ms: B1 for one pair of equal sides with reason, e.g. AB = CD (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal)
B1 for the other pair, BC = DA, and AC is a common side
B1 for a full proof concluding congruent with condition SSS (allow SAS or ASA if alternate angles are correctly used with reasons)
questions.tip: State the congruence condition at the end, e.g. 'congruent by SSS'.
steps: To prove congruence, find three matching facts and give a reason for each.
AB = CD and BC = DA, because opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal.
AC is a side of both triangles (common side).
Three pairs of equal sides means congruent by SSS.
Answer: AB = CD (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal). BC = DA (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal). AC is common to both triangles. So the triangles are congruent (SSS).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCD is a square. Point P lies outside the square so that triangle ABP is equilateral. Point Q lies outside the square so that triangle BCQ is equilateral.
Prove that AQ = CP.
questions.answer: AB = BC (sides of a square). BP = AB and BQ = BC (equilateral triangles), so BP = BQ. Angle ABQ = 90 + 60 = 150° and angle PBC = 60 + 90 = 150°. So triangles ABQ and PBC are congruent (SAS), so AQ = PC.
ms: B1 for AB = BC with reason (sides of a square are equal)
B1 for BQ = BP (equal to the sides of the square, as the triangles are equilateral)
B1 for angle ABQ = angle PBC = 150° (90° + 60°)
B1 for triangles ABQ and PBC congruent by SAS, therefore AQ = CP (corresponding sides of congruent triangles)
questions.tip: Pick the two triangles that contain AQ and CP. Show the included angle matches.
steps: Plan: show triangles ABQ and PBC are congruent, then AQ and CP are matching sides.
AB = BC (sides of a square). BP = AB and BQ = BC (sides of the equilateral triangles), so BP = BQ.
Angle ABQ = 90 + 60 = 150° and angle PBC = 60 + 90 = 150°, so the angles between the equal sides match.
Two sides and the included angle are equal, so the triangles are congruent (SAS), so AQ = PC.

Answer: AB = BC (sides of a square). BP = AB and BQ = BC (equilateral triangles), so BP = BQ. Angle ABQ = 90 + 60 = 150° and angle PBC = 60 + 90 = 150°. So triangles ABQ and PBC are congruent (SAS), so AQ = PC.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Two similar cylinders have volumes in the ratio 8 : 27. What is the ratio of their curved surface areas?
questions.tip: Cube root the volume ratio to get lengths, then square for areas.
steps: Volume ratio is the length ratio cubed, so cube root to get lengths: ∛8 : ∛27 = 2 : 3.
Area ratio is the length ratio squared: 2² : 3² = 4 : 9.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A right-angled triangle has shorter sides 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.tip: Square, add, then square root. Do not just add the sides.

questions.q: [Calculator] In triangle ABC, angle B = 90°, AC = 12 cm and angle A = 35°. Find BC to 3 significant figures.
ms: BC is opposite angle A and AC is the hypotenuse: BC = 12 sin 35° = 6.88 cm.
questions.tip: Label O, A, H from the given angle. 9.83 comes from using cos.
steps: Label from angle A: BC is opposite A, and AC is the hypotenuse (opposite the right angle at B).
Opposite and hypotenuse means SOH: sin 35° = BC/12.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the exact value of tan 60°?
questions.tip: Learn the exact values table: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.
steps: Use tan = sin ÷ cos with the exact values sin 60° = √3/2 and cos 60° = 1/2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle PQR has angle Q = 90°, angle P = 30° and PR = 10 cm.
(a) Find the exact length of QR.
(b) Find the exact length of PQ. Give your answer as a surd.
questions.tip: 'Exact' means leave it as a surd. Simplify √75 to 5√3.
steps: From angle P: QR is opposite, PQ is adjacent, PR = 10 is the hypotenuse.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A ladder leans against a vertical wall. The foot of the ladder is 4 m from the wall and the top is 7 m up the wall.
Work out the angle the ladder makes with the ground. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: Check your calculator is in degrees mode (D on screen).
steps: Draw the right-angled triangle. From the angle on the ground: opposite = 7 m (up the wall), adjacent = 4 m.
Opposite and adjacent means TOA: tan x = 7/4 = 1.75.

questions.q:
[Calculator] ABCDEFGH is a cuboid. The base ABCD is horizontal with AB = 8 cm and BC = 6 cm. The vertical edges AE, BF, CG and DH are each 5 cm long.
(a) Work out the length of the diagonal AG.
(b) Work out the angle between AG and the base ABCD.
Give your answers to 1 decimal place.
ms: M1 for tan θ = 5/10 (or sin θ = 5/11.18)
questions.tip: The angle with the base is between AG and AC (its projection on the base), not AB.
steps: 3D problem: find a right-angled triangle on the base first. AC is the diagonal of the base.
Triangle ACG has a right angle at C, with CG = 5 cm up. AG = √(10² + 5²) = √125 = 11.18... = 11.2 cm.
The angle with the base is angle GAC. tan θ = opposite/adjacent = 5/10 = 0.5.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A pyramid VABCD has a square base ABCD of side 6 cm. The apex V is vertically above the centre M of the base. Each sloping edge (VA, VB, VC, VD) is 9 cm.
(a) Work out the height VM.
(b) Work out the angle between VA and the base.
Give your answers to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for cos θ = √18/9 or tan θ = 7.94/4.243 or sin θ = 7.94/9
questions.tip: AM is half the diagonal of the base, not half the side (3 cm).
steps: M is the middle of the base diagonal, so find the diagonal first: AC = √(6² + 6²) = √72 = 8.485... cm.
AM is half of that: AM = √72 ÷ 2 = √18 = 4.243... cm.
Triangle VMA has a right angle at M with hypotenuse VA = 9. VM = √(9² - 18) = √(81 - 18) = √63 = 7.94 cm.
The angle between VA and the base is angle VAM. cos θ = AM/VA = √18/9 = 0.4714...

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In triangle ABC, angle ABC = 90°, AB = 4√3 cm and angle BAC = 30°.
Show that BC = 4 cm and find the exact length of AC.
ms: B1 for AC = 8 cm (from cos 30°, or √(48 + 16) = √64)
questions.tip: Use the exact value 1/√3 for tan 30° and simplify √3/√3 = 1.
steps: From angle A = 30°: BC is opposite, AB = 4√3 is adjacent, so use tan.
AC is the hypotenuse, so use cos: AC = 4√3 ÷ cos 30° = 4√3 ÷ (√3/2) = 4 × 2 = 8 cm.

questions.q: [Calculator] In triangle ABC, AB = 7 cm, BC = 9 cm and angle ABC = 50°. Find AC to 3 significant figures.
ms: Cosine rule: AC² = 7² + 9² - 2 × 7 × 9 × cos 50° = 49.0..., AC = 7.00 cm.
questions.tip: Remember the square root at the end (49.0 is AC²), and the minus sign in the rule (14.5 uses +).
steps: Two sides and the angle between them, finding the third side: use the cosine rule.

questions.q: [Calculator] Triangle PQR has PQ = 8 cm, PR = 11 cm and angle QPR = 35°. What is its area to 3 s.f.?
questions.tip: Use ½ab sin C with the angle between the two sides. Forgetting the ½ gives 50.5.
steps: Two sides and the angle between them, finding area: use Area = ½ab sin C.

questions.q:
[Calculator] In triangle ABC, angle A = 40°, angle B = 65° and the side AC = 12 cm.
Work out the length of BC. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.tip: Pair each side with the angle opposite it. AC is opposite angle B.
steps: You know two angles and a side, so use the sine rule. Match each side with the angle opposite it.
BC is opposite angle A (40°). AC = 12 is opposite angle B (65°).

questions.q:
[Calculator] In triangle PQR, PR = 10 cm, QR = 8.5 cm and angle QPR = 48°. Angle PQR is acute.
Work out the size of angle PQR. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: Put the angles on top when finding an angle: sin Q/q = sin P/p.
steps: Use the sine rule to find an angle. Pair each side with its opposite angle.
PR = 10 is opposite angle Q. QR = 8.5 is opposite angle P = 48°.
Q = sin⁻¹(0.8742...) = 60.96...°, which is 61.0° to 1 d.p. (we are told it is acute).

questions.q:
[Calculator] A triangle has sides of length 5 cm, 7 cm and 9 cm.
Work out the size of the largest angle. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: The largest angle is opposite the longest side (9 cm). A negative cosine gives an obtuse angle.
steps: The largest angle is opposite the longest side (9 cm). Use the cosine rule rearranged for an angle.
cos is negative, so the angle is obtuse. θ = cos⁻¹(-0.1) = 95.73...° = 95.7°.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A ship sails 12 km from port A on a bearing of 070° to point B.
It then sails 8 km on a bearing of 160° to point C.
(a) Show that angle ABC = 90°.
(b) Work out the distance AC.
(c) Work out the bearing of C from A.
Give lengths to 3 s.f. and the bearing to the nearest degree.
questions.answer: (a) Bearing of A from B is 250°, 250 - 160 = 90°  (b) 14.4 km  (c) 104°
ms: B1 for showing angle ABC = 90°, e.g. bearing of A from B = 070 + 180 = 250°, and 250 - 160 = 90°
questions.tip: Bearings are measured clockwise from north and written with three figures. Draw a north line at every point.
steps: (a) The bearing of A from B is the back bearing: 070 + 180 = 250°.
At B, the path to C is 160° and the path back to A is 250°, so the angle between them is 250 - 160 = 90°.
(b) Right angle at B, so use Pythagoras: AC = √(12² + 8²) = √208 = 14.42... = 14.4 km.
(c) In the triangle, angle BAC = tan⁻¹(8/12) = 33.69...°.
C is clockwise from B as seen from A, so bearing = 070 + 33.69... = 103.69... = 104°.
Answer: (a) Bearing of A from B is 250°, 250 - 160 = 90°  (b) 14.4 km  (c) 104°

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The bearing of Q from P is 125°. What is the bearing of P from Q?
questions.tip: Add 180° if the bearing is under 180°, subtract 180° if over.
steps: A back bearing points the opposite way, so add or subtract 180°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle ABC has area 45 cm². AB = 9 cm and angle BAC = 30°.
Work out the length of AC.
ms: M1 for using sin 30° = 1/2, giving 9/4 × AC = 45
questions.tip: Use the exact value sin 30° = 1/2 on a non-calculator paper.
steps: Use Area = ½ × AB × AC × sin A, because you know the area, one side and the angle between the two sides.
That is 9/4 × AC = 45, so AC = 45 × 4 ÷ 9 = 20 cm.

questions.q:
[Calculator] ABCD is a quadrilateral. AB = 6 cm, BC = 8 cm, angle ABC = 110°, AD = 7 cm and angle CAD = 40°.
Work out the area of ABCD. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for area ABC = ½ × 6 × 8 × sin 110° (= 22.55)
questions.tip: Keep the unrounded value of AC in your calculator for the next step to avoid accuracy errors.
steps: Split the quadrilateral along AC into triangles ABC and ACD. You need AC first.
Area ACD = ½ × 11.525... × 7 × sin 40° = 25.93... cm². Keep the full AC value to avoid rounding errors.

questions.q: [Calculator] You know two sides of a triangle and the angle between them. You want the third side. Which do you use?
ms: Two sides and the included angle (SAS) to find the opposite side needs the cosine rule a² = b² + c² - 2bc cos A.
questions.tip: The sine rule needs an angle and its opposite side as a pair.
steps: Ask: what do I know, and what do I want? Here: two sides plus the angle between them, and you want the third side.
The sine rule needs a side with its opposite angle, which you do not have. ½ab sin C gives area, not a side.
The cosine rule a² = b² + c² - 2bc cos A uses exactly two sides and the included angle.

questions.q: [Calculator] A sector has radius 9 cm and angle 40°. What is the arc length to 3 s.f.?
questions.tip: Arc length uses 2πr (circumference). 28.3 is the sector area.
steps: Arc length = (angle/360) × 2πr, the fraction of the full circumference.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A circle has radius 6 cm. What is its exact area?
questions.tip: Square the radius, not the diameter.
steps: Area of a circle = πr². Exact means leave π in.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A sector of a circle has radius 12 cm and angle 150°.
Work out the area of the sector. Give your answer in terms of π.
questions.tip: Simplify 150/360 to 5/12 to make the arithmetic easy.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A sector has radius 7 cm and angle 100°.
Work out the perimeter of the sector. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: The perimeter includes the two radii as well as the arc.
steps: The perimeter of a sector is the curved arc plus the two straight radii.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A sector has radius 6 cm and arc length 11 cm.
Work out the angle of the sector, to the nearest degree.
questions.tip: Form an equation with θ and rearrange. Do not guess and check.
steps: Set up the arc length formula with the angle θ unknown: θ/360 × 2π × 6 = 11.
θ = 105.04...°, which is 105° to the nearest degree.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A chord AB cuts a circle of centre O and radius 10 cm. Angle AOB = 60°.
Work out the area of the minor segment cut off by AB. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for triangle area ½ × 10 × 10 × sin 60° (= 43.30)
questions.tip: Segment = sector - triangle. Use ½ab sin C for the triangle.
steps: Segment = sector minus the triangle OAB.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A sector has angle 60° and area 24π cm².
Work out the exact perimeter of the sector. Give your answer in the form a + bπ.
questions.tip: Find r first. The perimeter is 2r + arc.
steps: First find the radius from the area: 60/360 × πr² = 24π.
1/6 × r² = 24, so r² = 144 and r = 12 cm.

questions.q: [Calculator] A square has side 8 cm. A quarter circle of radius 8 cm is drawn inside it, centred at one corner. What is the area of the square NOT inside the quarter circle, to 3 s.f.?
questions.tip: The quarter circle uses ¼πr², with r = 8 (the side of the square). Subtract it from the square: 114 comes from adding instead.
steps: Shaded area = square minus quarter circle.
Square = 8 × 8 = 64 cm². Quarter circle = ¼ × π × 8² = 16π = 50.265... cm².

questions.q: [Calculator] A cone has radius 5 cm and perpendicular height 12 cm. What is its volume to 3 s.f.?
questions.tip: Do not forget the ⅓. 942 is the volume of a cylinder with the same dimensions.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A sphere has radius 3 cm. What is its exact volume?
questions.tip: Cube the radius first (27), then multiply by 4/3.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A cone has radius 6 cm and slant height 10 cm. What is its total surface area?
ms: Curved area = πrl = 60π, base = πr² = 36π, total = 96π cm².
questions.tip: 'Total' surface area includes the circular base. Curved surface uses slant height l, not h.
steps: Total surface area of a cone = curved part + circular base.
Curved = πrl = π × 6 × 10 = 60π. Base = πr² = π × 6² = 36π.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A solid hemisphere has radius 4 cm.
Work out its total surface area. Give your answer in terms of π.
ms: M1 for adding the flat circle π × 4² (= 16π)
questions.tip: A solid hemisphere has a flat circular face too. Half of 4πr² alone is only 32π.
steps: A solid hemisphere has a curved half-sphere surface and a flat circle on the bottom. Do not forget the flat face.
Sphere surface = 4πr², so curved part = ½ × 4π × 4² = ½ × 64π = 32π.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A pyramid has a square base of side 6 cm and a perpendicular height of 10 cm.
Work out the volume of the pyramid.
questions.tip: Volume of a pyramid = ⅓ × base area × height. Use the perpendicular height, not a slant edge.
steps: Volume of a pyramid = ⅓ × base area × height.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A frustum is made by removing a small cone from the top of a large cone. The large cone has base radius 10 cm and perpendicular height 24 cm. The small cone removed has base radius 5 cm and height 12 cm.
Work out the volume of the frustum. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for volume of large cone ⅓ × π × 10² × 24 (= 800π = 2513.3)
M1 for volume of small cone ⅓ × π × 5² × 12 (= 100π = 314.2)
questions.tip: A frustum is large cone minus small cone. You cannot use the average radius.
steps: Frustum = big cone minus small cone.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted down and recast into a solid cylinder of radius 4 cm.
Work out the height of the cylinder.
questions.tip: Equal volumes: set the two formulas equal. π cancels, so leave it as π.
steps: Melting keeps the volume the same, so sphere volume = cylinder volume.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cone has base radius 5 cm. The curved surface area of the cone is 65π cm².
Work out the volume of the cone. Give your answer in terms of π.
questions.tip: The volume needs the perpendicular height, so use Pythagoras on the slant height.
steps: Curved surface area = πrl, so use it to find the slant height l.
π × 5 × l = 65π, so 5l = 65 and l = 13 cm.
Volume needs the vertical height. Pythagoras: h = √(13² - 5²) = √(169 - 25) = √144 = 12 cm.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A solid is made from a cylinder with a hemisphere on top. The cylinder and hemisphere both have radius 3 cm. The cylinder has height h cm.
The total volume of the solid is 45π cm³.
Work out the value of h.
ms: M1 for cylinder volume π × 3² × h = 9πh
M1 for hemisphere volume ½ × 4/3 × π × 3³ = 18π
questions.tip: Halve the sphere volume for the hemisphere. Divide every term by π to simplify.
steps: 9πh + 18π = 45π. Divide by π: 9h + 18 = 45, so 9h = 27 and h = 3.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the locus of points that are exactly 4 cm from a fixed point P?
options: A circle of radius 4 cm centred on P
A circle of diameter 4 cm centred on P
ms: All points a fixed distance from a point form a circle with that radius.
questions.tip: Radius, not diameter, is the fixed distance.
steps: A locus is the path of all points that obey a rule.
Every point exactly 4 cm from P lies on a circle with centre P and radius 4 cm (radius, not diameter).
Answer: A circle of radius 4 cm centred on P

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the locus of points equidistant from two fixed points A and B?
options: A circle centred at the midpoint of AB
ms: Points the same distance from A and B lie on the perpendicular bisector of AB.
questions.tip: Equidistant from two POINTS = perpendicular bisector. Equidistant from two LINES = angle bisector.
steps: Equidistant means the same distance from A as from B.
Those points form the line that cuts AB in half at right angles: the perpendicular bisector.
Answer: The perpendicular bisector of AB

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the locus of points equidistant from two lines that meet at a point?
options: A line parallel to one of the lines
The bisector of the angle between the lines
ms: Points equidistant from two intersecting lines lie on the angle bisector.
questions.tip: Do not confuse lines with points.
steps: Points the same distance from two lines that meet sit exactly halfway between them in angle terms.
That line splits the angle between the lines in half: the angle bisector.
Answer: The bisector of the angle between the lines

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Describe how to construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment AB using only a ruler and a pair of compasses.
questions.answer: Set compasses to more than half of AB. Draw arcs above and below AB from A. With the same radius, draw arcs from B to cross the first arcs. Join the two crossing points with a straight line.
ms: B1 for compasses set to more than half the length of AB
B1 for arcs drawn from both A and B with the SAME radius, crossing above and below the line
B1 for joining the two intersection points with a ruler (leave construction arcs showing)
questions.tip: Always leave your construction arcs visible. Without arcs, a correct line scores zero.
steps: Open the compasses to more than half the length of AB, otherwise the arcs will not meet.
Put the point on A and draw arcs above and below AB.
Keep the same radius, put the point on B and draw arcs that cross the first two.
Join the two crossing points with a ruler. Leave the arcs showing.
Answer: Set compasses to more than half of AB. Draw arcs above and below AB from A. With the same radius, draw arcs from B to cross the first arcs. Join the two crossing points with a straight line.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Describe how to construct the bisector of angle ABC using only a ruler and compasses.
questions.answer: With compasses centred on B, draw an arc crossing BA at P and BC at Q. With the same radius, draw arcs from P and from Q that cross at R. Draw the line from B through R.
ms: B1 for an arc centred at B cutting both arms of the angle
B1 for equal-radius arcs from the two crossing points, intersecting inside the angle
B1 for joining B to the intersection point
questions.tip: The two arcs from P and Q must use the same radius.
steps: Put the compass point on B and draw an arc that crosses both arms of the angle, at P (on BA) and Q (on BC).
Keep the same radius. Draw an arc from P and an arc from Q so they cross inside the angle at R.
Draw a straight line from B through R. That line bisects the angle.
Answer: With compasses centred on B, draw an arc crossing BA at P and BC at Q. With the same radius, draw arcs from P and from Q that cross at R. Draw the line from B through R.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A rectangular garden ABCD has AB = 10 m and BC = 6 m. A tree is to be planted so that it is:
- closer to AB than to AD, and
- less than 4 m from C.
Describe fully the region where the tree can be planted.
questions.answer: The region inside the rectangle that is on the AB side of the bisector of angle DAB (the line from A at 45° to AB and AD), and inside the circle of radius 4 m centred at C.
ms: B1 for the bisector of angle DAB (angle at A between AB and AD), a line from A at 45° to AB
B1 for an arc/circle of radius 4 m centred at C
B1 for the correct region identified: on the AB side of the angle bisector and inside the circle centred at C
questions.tip: 'Closer to a line' uses an angle bisector. 'Less than 4 m from a point' means inside a circle.
steps: Each condition gives a locus. 'Closer to AB than to AD' uses the angle bisector of angle DAB, where AB and AD meet.
That bisector is a line from A at 45° to both sides. Points closer to AB are on the AB side of it.
'Less than 4 m from C' means inside a circle of radius 4 m centred at C.
The tree must satisfy both, so the region is where these overlap inside the garden.
Answer: The region inside the rectangle that is on the AB side of the bisector of angle DAB (the line from A at 45° to AB and AD), and inside the circle of radius 4 m centred at C.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Describe how to construct the perpendicular from a point P to a line L, where P is not on L, using a ruler and compasses.
questions.answer: With centre P draw an arc cutting L at two points, A and B. From A and from B, with the same radius, draw arcs crossing on the other side of L at Q. Join P to Q.
ms: B1 for an arc centred at P crossing L at two points
B1 for equal arcs from those two points intersecting (on the opposite side of L to P)
B1 for joining P to the intersection point
questions.tip: This is the perpendicular bisector of the two points where your first arc meets L.
steps: Put the compass point on P and draw an arc that cuts L at two points, A and B.
Keep the same radius. From A and from B, draw arcs that cross on the other side of L, at Q.
Join P to Q with a ruler. This line meets L at 90°.
Answer: With centre P draw an arc cutting L at two points, A and B. From A and from B, with the same radius, draw arcs crossing on the other side of L at Q. Join P to Q.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A goat is tied to the corner A of a square shed ABCD with side 4 m, using a rope of length 6 m. The goat is outside the shed and cannot go through it.
Describe the region the goat can reach. Calculate the area of this region in terms of π.
questions.answer: Three-quarters of a circle of radius 6 m centred at A, plus two quarter circles of radius 2 m centred at B and D. Area = 27π + π + π = 29π m².
ms: B1 for ¾ of a circle radius 6 centred at A: ¾ × π × 36 = 27π
B1 for recognising the rope wraps round corners B and D, giving quarter circles of radius 2 m (π each)
questions.tip: The rope wraps around the corners of the shed, leaving 6 - 4 = 2 m of rope at B and D.
steps: From A the goat can swing round everywhere except inside the shed's 90° corner, so it covers ¾ of a circle of radius 6 m.
The rope can also bend round corners B and D. 6 - 4 = 2 m of rope is left, giving a quarter circle of radius 2 m at each.
Each quarter circle = ¼ × π × 2² = π, so two of them = 2π.
Answer: Three-quarters of a circle of radius 6 m centred at A, plus two quarter circles of radius 2 m centred at B and D. Area = 27π + π + π = 29π m².

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Describe how to construct an angle of 60° at point A on a line, using ruler and compasses only.
questions.answer: Draw an arc centred on A crossing the line at B. With the same radius, draw an arc centred on B crossing the first arc at C. Join A to C. Angle CAB = 60°.
ms: B1 for an arc centred on A and an arc of the same radius centred on the crossing point B
B1 for joining A to the intersection, forming an equilateral triangle so the angle is 60°
questions.tip: The radius must stay the same, because the method makes an equilateral triangle.
steps: The trick is to build an equilateral triangle, because all its angles are 60°.
Draw an arc centred on A crossing the line at B.
Same radius: draw an arc centred on B crossing the first arc at C. Now AB = BC = AC.
Join A to C. Angle CAB = 60°.
Answer: Draw an arc centred on A crossing the line at B. With the same radius, draw an arc centred on B crossing the first arc at C. Join A to C. Angle CAB = 60°.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The point (3, -2) is reflected in the line y = x. What are its new coordinates?
ms: Reflection in y = x swaps the coordinates: (3, -2) becomes (-2, 3).
questions.tip: Reflection in y = -x swaps and changes both signs, giving (2, -3).
steps: Reflecting in y = x swaps the x and y coordinates: (x, y) becomes (y, x).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The point (4, 1) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. What is its image?
ms: 90° clockwise about the origin maps (x, y) to (y, -x), so (4, 1) → (1, -4).
questions.tip: (-1, 4) is the anticlockwise rotation. Use tracing paper in the exam.
steps: Rule for 90° clockwise about the origin: (x, y) goes to (y, -x).
Sense check: (4, 1) is in the top right; a quarter turn clockwise moves it to the bottom right.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Triangle A has a vertex at (2, 4). It is enlarged with scale factor -2 and centre of enlargement the origin. Where does this vertex go?
ms: Negative scale factor: multiply the vector from the centre by -2, so (2, 4) → (-4, -8).
questions.tip: A negative scale factor puts the image on the opposite side of the centre and upside down.
steps: Centre is the origin, so multiply both coordinates by the scale factor -2.
The negative flips the point to the other side of the centre.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Shape P has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 2). Shape Q has vertices (4, -2), (6, -2) and (4, -1).
Describe fully the single transformation that maps P onto Q.
ms: B1 for vector (3 over -3), written as a column vector
questions.tip: Write the word 'translation' and a column vector. 'Moved 3 right and 3 down' only gets 1 mark.
steps: The shapes are the same size and the same way round, so it is a translation.
Track one vertex: (1, 1) goes to (4, -2). x changes by 4 - 1 = 3, y changes by -2 - 1 = -3.
Check another: (3, 1) to (6, -2) also moves 3 right and 3 down.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle A has vertices (2, 2), (6, 2) and (2, 6). Triangle B has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 3).
Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle A onto triangle B.
questions.tip: A fractional scale factor makes the shape smaller. You need all three facts: enlargement, scale factor, centre.
steps: B is smaller but the same shape, so it is an enlargement.
Side length goes from 6 - 2 = 4 to 3 - 1 = 2, so scale factor = 2 ÷ 4 = 1/2.
Every coordinate halves, e.g. (6, 2) goes to (3, 1), so the centre is the origin (0, 0).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Point P has coordinates (5, 7). P is enlarged by scale factor -1/2 with centre of enlargement (1, 1).
Work out the coordinates of the image of P.
ms: M1 for the vector from the centre to P: (4, 6)
M1 for multiplying by -1/2 to get (-2, -3)
questions.tip: Always work from the centre, not from the origin, and add the scaled vector back onto the centre.
steps: Work from the centre. Vector from centre (1, 1) to P (5, 7) is (5 - 1, 7 - 1) = (4, 6).
Multiply by the scale factor -1/2: (4 × -1/2, 6 × -1/2) = (-2, -3). The minus sends it the opposite way.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Shape A is reflected in the line x = 1 to give shape B. Shape B is then reflected in the line x = 4 to give shape C.
Describe fully the single transformation that maps shape A onto shape C.
ms: B1 for a horizontal translation to the right
B1 for vector (6, 0) (twice the distance between the mirror lines, 2 × 3)
questions.tip: Two reflections in parallel lines give a translation of twice the gap between the lines. Test with a point, e.g. (0, 0) → (2, 0) → (6, 0).
steps: Two reflections in parallel mirror lines always make a translation.
The distance between the lines x = 1 and x = 4 is 4 - 1 = 3.
The translation is twice that distance, in the direction from the first line to the second: 2 × 3 = 6 to the right.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle T has vertices (1, 2), (3, 2) and (3, 5). It is rotated 180° about the point (2, 0).
Write down the coordinates of the vertices of the image.
ms: M1 for using (x, y) → (2 × 2 - x, 2 × 0 - y) = (4 - x, -y), or a correct rotation of at least one vertex
questions.tip: A rotation of 180° about (a, b) sends (x, y) to (2a - x, 2b - y).
steps: A 180° turn about (2, 0) sends each point to the opposite side of the centre, the same distance away.
Rule: (x, y) goes to (2 × 2 - x, 2 × 0 - y) = (4 - x, -y).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] a = (3, -1) and b = (-2, 4) as column vectors. What is 2a + b?
questions.tip: Multiply both components by 2 before adding.
steps: Work on the top and bottom numbers separately.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the magnitude of the vector (5, -12)?
questions.tip: Squaring -12 gives +144. The magnitude is always positive.
steps: Magnitude means length. Use Pythagoras on the two components.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] OA = a and OB = b. What is the vector AB?
ms: AB = AO + OB = -a + b = b - a.
questions.tip: Go from A back to O (-a), then O to B (+b).
steps: To get from A to B, go A to O then O to B.
A to O is backwards along a, so it is -a. O to B is b.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OAB is a triangle. OA = a and OB = b. M is the midpoint of AB.
Find the vector OM in terms of a and b. Give your answer in its simplest form.
ms: M1 for OM = a + ½(b - a)
A1 for ½a + ½b (or ½(a + b))
questions.tip: Write a route from O to M using vectors you know, then simplify.
steps: Find a route from O to M through known points: O to A, then halfway along AB.
OM = a + ½(b - a) = a + ½b - ½a.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OAB is a triangle. OA = a and OB = b. P is the point on AB such that AP : PB = 1 : 3.
Find OP in terms of a and b. Give your answer in its simplest form.
ms: M1 for OP = a + ¼(b - a)
questions.tip: AP : PB = 1 : 3 means AP is 1/4 of AB, not 1/3.
steps: AP : PB = 1 : 3 means P is 1 of 4 parts along AB, so AP = ¼AB.
AB = b - a, so AP = ¼(b - a).
OP = OA + AP = a + ¼(b - a) = a + ¼b - ¼a.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OABC is a parallelogram with OA = a and OC = c. M is the midpoint of AB. N is the point on OB such that ON : NB = 2 : 1.
Prove that C, N and M lie on a straight line.
questions.answer: OB = a + c. CN = -c + ⅔(a + c) = ⅔a - ⅓c. CM = -c + a + ½c = a - ½c. CM = 3/2 × CN, so CN and CM are parallel and share point C, so C, N and M are collinear.
ms: M1 for CN = -c + ⅔(a + c) = ⅔a - ⅓c
M1 for CM = -c + a + ½c = a - ½c (using AB = c, so AM = ½c)
M1 for showing one is a multiple of the other: CN = ⅔(a - ½c) = ⅔ CM
A1 for conclusion: CN and CM are parallel and have the common point C, so C, N, M are on a straight line
questions.tip: To prove collinear you need BOTH: one vector is a multiple of the other, AND they share a point.
steps: To show three points are on a line, show CN and CM are multiples of each other (parallel) and share point C.
OB = OA + AB = a + c, since AB = OC in a parallelogram. ON = ⅔(a + c).
CN = CO + ON = -c + ⅔a + ⅔c = ⅔a - ⅓c.
CM = CO + OA + AM = -c + a + ½c = a - ½c.
CN = ⅔(a - ½c) = ⅔CM, so they are parallel. They both start at C, so C, N and M lie on one line.
Answer: OB = a + c. CN = -c + ⅔(a + c) = ⅔a - ⅓c. CM = -c + a + ½c = a - ½c. CM = 3/2 × CN, so CN and CM are parallel and share point C, so C, N and M are collinear.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OAB is a triangle with OA = a and OB = b. X is the midpoint of OA and Y is the midpoint of OB.
Prove that XY is parallel to AB and half its length.
questions.answer: AB = b - a. XY = -½a + ½b = ½(b - a) = ½AB. So XY is parallel to AB and half its length.
ms: M1 for XY = XO + OY = -½a + ½b
M1 for writing XY = ½(b - a)
A1 for concluding XY = ½AB, so parallel and half the length
questions.tip: Factorise to show one vector is a scalar multiple of the other, then write a conclusion in words.
steps: Write AB and XY in terms of a and b, then compare.
XY = ½(b - a) = ½AB. Being a multiple of AB means parallel, and ½ means half the length.
Answer: AB = b - a. XY = -½a + ½b = ½(b - a) = ½AB. So XY is parallel to AB and half its length.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The vectors p = (2, k) and q = (6, 9) are parallel.
Find the value of k.
questions.tip: Parallel vectors are scalar multiples of each other: compare the x and y components with the same multiplier.
steps: Parallel vectors are multiples of each other.
Then the bottom: 3 × k = 9, so k = 3.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which vector is parallel to 2a - 3b?
ms: -4a + 6b = -2(2a - 3b), a scalar multiple, so it is parallel.
questions.tip: Parallel means a multiple of the whole vector; both coefficients must scale by the same number.
steps: The others do not keep the same ratio of a to b with the same signs.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A spinner can land on red, blue, green or yellow. P(red) = 0.35, P(blue) = 0.2, P(green) = 0.15. What is P(yellow)?
questions.tip: 0.7 is the total of the given probabilities, not the missing one.
steps: All the probabilities must add up to 1.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The probability that a biased coin lands on heads is 0.12. It is thrown 250 times. What is the expected number of heads?
questions.tip: Multiply the probability by the number of trials.
steps: Expected number = probability × number of trials.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A dice is rolled 80 times. It lands on six 22 times.
(a) Work out the relative frequency of rolling a six.
(b) Is the dice likely to be fair? Give a reason.
questions.answer: (a) 22/80 = 0.275  (b) Probably biased: 0.275 is much higher than 1/6 ≈ 0.167 (but more rolls would give a more reliable estimate).
ms: B1 for a comparison with 1/6 (≈ 0.167) and a conclusion, e.g. likely to be biased as 0.275 is much bigger than 1/6
questions.tip: Compare the relative frequency to the theoretical probability with actual numbers.
steps: (a) Relative frequency = times it happened ÷ total trials = 22/80 = 0.275.
(b) A fair dice gives a six with probability 1/6 ≈ 0.167, so we would expect about 80 ÷ 6 ≈ 13 sixes.
22 sixes (0.275) is a lot more than that, so the dice is probably biased. More rolls would make the estimate more reliable.
Answer: (a) 22/80 = 0.275  (b) Probably biased: 0.275 is much higher than 1/6 ≈ 0.167 (but more rolls would give a more reliable estimate).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Two fair six-sided dice are rolled and the scores are added. What is the probability of a total of 8?
questions.tip: Use a sample space diagram. Totals are not all equally likely, so 1/11 is wrong.
steps: Two dice give 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely outcomes.
List the ways to make 8: (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2). That is 5 ways.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A code is made of 2 letters (A to Z) followed by 3 digits (0 to 9). Letters and digits may repeat.
How many different codes are possible?
questions.tip: Use the product rule: multiply the number of choices for each position.
steps: Use the product rule: multiply the number of choices for each position.
Each letter has 26 choices, each digit has 10 choices.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains n red counters and 5 blue counters only. A counter is taken at random. The probability it is red is 3/8.
Find the value of n.
questions.tip: The total number of counters is n + 5, not 5.
steps: Total counters = n + 5, so P(red) = n/(n + 5).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Events A and B are mutually exclusive. P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.25. What is P(A or B)?
ms: For mutually exclusive events, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) = 0.65.
questions.tip: 0.1 is P(A) × P(B), which is for independent events happening together.
steps: Mutually exclusive means they cannot both happen, so just add.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 200 students were asked how they travel to school. 85 walk. Of the students who do not walk, 40% come by bus and the rest come by car.
A student is chosen at random. Work out the probability that the student comes by car.
questions.tip: A frequency tree helps. 60% of the non-walkers, not 60% of everyone.
steps: 40% of them take the bus, so 60% come by car: 115 × 0.6 = 69.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A bag has 3 red and 5 green balls. A ball is taken, replaced, and a second ball is taken. What is P(both red)?
questions.tip: With replacement the denominators stay at 8. 3/28 is without replacement.
steps: With replacement, the bag is the same for the second pick, so both picks have P(red) = 3/8.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A bag has 3 red and 5 green balls. Two balls are taken without replacement. What is P(both red)?
questions.tip: Without replacement, one fewer red AND one fewer ball in total for the second pick.
steps: Without replacement, the second pick has one fewer red and one fewer ball.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 3 red sweets and 5 green sweets. Kai takes a sweet at random and eats it. He then takes another sweet at random.
Work out the probability that he takes one sweet of each colour.
questions.tip: There are two ways to get one of each: red then green, or green then red.
steps: One of each can happen two ways: red then green, or green then red. He eats the first, so it is without replacement.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A box has 6 working bulbs and 4 faulty bulbs. Three bulbs are taken at random without replacement.
Work out the probability that at least one of the bulbs works.
questions.tip: 'At least one' is easiest as 1 - P(none).
steps: 'At least one' is easier the other way round: 1 - P(none work), i.e. 1 - P(all faulty).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The probability that Jo passes her driving theory test is 0.7. The probability that she passes her practical test is 0.4. The two events are independent.
Work out the probability that she passes exactly one of the tests.
questions.tip: Exactly one: pass first and fail second, or fail first and pass second.
steps: Exactly one can happen two ways: pass theory only, or pass practical only.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A box contains n pens. 5 of the pens are black. Two pens are taken at random without replacement.
The probability that both pens are black is 5/33.
(a) Show that n² - n - 132 = 0.
(b) Work out the value of n.
ms: A1 for rearranging correctly to n² - n - 132 = 0 (convincing, no errors)
questions.tip: For 'show that' every step must appear. Reject the negative solution with a reason.
steps: 660 = 5n(n - 1), divide by 5: 132 = n² - n, so n² - n - 132 = 0.
You cannot have a negative number of pens, so n = 12.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 4 red, 5 blue and 3 yellow counters. Three counters are taken at random without replacement.
Work out the probability that the three counters are all different colours.
ms: M1 for one correct product, e.g. 4/12 × 5/11 × 3/10 (= 60/1320)
M1 for recognising there are 6 orders
questions.tip: Multiply one ordered product by the number of orders (3 × 2 × 1 = 6).
steps: All different means one red, one blue, one yellow, picked in any order.
The three colours can come in 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 orders, each with the same probability.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What does A ∩ B mean?
options: Elements in A or B or both
Elements in A but not B
Elements in both A and B
ms: ∩ is intersection: elements in both sets.
questions.tip: ∪ is union (A or B or both); ∩ is intersection (both).
steps: ∩ is the intersection symbol (think of it as 'and').
A ∩ B is everything that is in A and also in B.
Answer: Elements in both A and B

questions.q: [Non-calculator] ξ = {1, 2, 3, ..., 10}. A = {even numbers}, B = {multiples of 3}. Which is A ∪ B?
ms: A = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}, B = {3, 6, 9}. The union contains everything in either: {2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10}.
questions.tip: List each set first. Do not count 6 twice.
steps: ∪ means union (think 'or'): everything in A or B or both, written once each.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] There are 60 students in a year group. 35 study French, 28 study Spanish and 10 study neither.
(a) Work out how many study both French and Spanish.
(b) A student is chosen at random. Find P(F ∩ S').
ms: M1 for 60 - 10 = 50 study at least one
questions.tip: F ∩ S' means in F and NOT in S, so French only.
steps: 35 + 28 = 63, which is 13 more than 50. Those 13 were counted twice, so 13 study both.
(b) F ∩ S' means French but not Spanish: 35 - 13 = 22.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] In a Venn diagram, 22 people are in F only, 13 are in F ∩ S, 15 are in S only and 10 are in neither. A person who is in F is chosen at random. What is the probability they are also in S?
ms: Given F: the total is 22 + 13 = 35, and 13 of these are in S, so 13/35.
questions.tip: 'Given F' changes the denominator to the number in F, not 60.
steps: 'A person in F is chosen' means we only look inside the F circle. This is conditional probability.
People in F = F only + both = 22 + 13 = 35.
Of those, 13 are also in S, so P = 13/35.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] In a Venn diagram for sets A and B: A only has 7, A ∩ B has 4, B only has 9, and outside both has 5. How many elements are in A' ∪ B?
ms: A' ∪ B = everything not in A, plus all of B: 9 + 5 + 4 = 18 (everything except A only).
questions.tip: A' ∪ B is everything except 'A only'. Total 25 - 7 = 18.
steps: A' is everything outside A: B only (9) and outside both (5).
A' ∪ B adds all of B, which brings in A ∩ B (4).
Total = 9 + 5 + 4 = 18. Only 'A only' (7) is left out.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 50 people were asked whether they own a bike (B) or a car (C).
The number who own a bike only is 3x. The number who own both is x. The number who own a car only is 2x + 1. 7 people own neither.
(a) Find x.
(b) A person who owns a car is chosen at random. Find the probability they also own a bike.
ms: M1 for number who own a car = 7 + 15 = 22
questions.tip: The 'given' condition (owns a car) sets the denominator: both + car only.
steps: All four regions add to 50: 3x + x + (2x + 1) + 7 = 50.
Of these 22, 7 also own a bike, so P = 7/22.

questions.q:
[Calculator] P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.15.
(a) Find P(A ∪ B).
(b) Find P(A | B), the probability of A given B.
questions.tip: Draw a Venn diagram with probabilities: fill the intersection first.
steps: (a) Adding P(A) and P(B) counts the overlap twice, so take it off once: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B).
(b) Given B, only look inside B: P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) ÷ P(B) = 0.15 ÷ 0.4 = 0.375.

questions.q:
[Calculator] P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.6 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.2.
Are A and B independent? Give a reason.
questions.answer: No. P(A) × P(B) = 0.18, which is not equal to P(A ∩ B) = 0.2.
questions.tip: The test for independence: does P(A) × P(B) equal P(A ∩ B)?
steps: Test: A and B are independent only if P(A) × P(B) = P(A ∩ B).
But P(A ∩ B) = 0.2, and 0.18 is not 0.2, so they are not independent.
Answer: No. P(A) × P(B) = 0.18, which is not equal to P(A ∩ B) = 0.2.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A two-way table shows 30 students: 12 boys like football, 6 boys do not; 5 girls like football, 7 girls do not. A girl is chosen at random. What is the probability she likes football?
ms: There are 5 + 7 = 12 girls; 5 like football, so 5/12.
questions.tip: 'A girl is chosen' means the denominator is the number of girls.
steps: We know it is a girl, so only count the girls.
Girls = 5 + 7 = 12, and 5 of them like football.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] P(A ∩ B) = 0.12 and P(B) = 0.3. What is P(A | B)?
questions.tip: Divide by the probability of the condition, do not multiply.
steps: P(A | B) means the probability of A, given B has happened. Formula: P(A ∩ B) ÷ P(B).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 80 people were asked if they prefer tea or coffee.
45 of them were adults, and the rest were teenagers. 28 adults prefer coffee. In total, 40 people prefer tea.
(a) Complete a two-way table and find how many teenagers prefer tea.
(b) A person who prefers tea is chosen at random. Find the probability that they are a teenager.
ms: M1 for adults who prefer tea = 45 - 28 = 17
A1 for teenagers who prefer tea = 40 - 17 = 23
M1 for denominator 40 (those who prefer tea)
questions.tip: Read 'a person who prefers tea is chosen' as the condition: use only the tea column.
steps: Fill in the two-way table one gap at a time. Adults who prefer tea = 45 - 28 = 17.
Total tea = 40, so teenagers who prefer tea = 40 - 17 = 23.
(b) We know the person prefers tea, so the total is 40, not 80.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The probability that it rains on a given day is 0.3.
If it rains, the probability that Leon is late for school is 0.4. If it does not rain, the probability that he is late is 0.1.
(a) Work out the probability that Leon is late on a given day.
(b) Given that Leon is late, work out the probability that it rained.
questions.tip: 'Given that he is late' means divide by P(late), not multiply.
steps: Draw a tree: rain (0.3) or no rain (0.7), then late or not late on each branch.
Rain and late: 0.3 × 0.4 = 0.12. No rain and late: 0.7 × 0.1 = 0.07.
(b) Given late, the total is now 0.19. The rainy part of that is 0.12, so P = 0.12 ÷ 0.19 = 12/19 = 0.632.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Two fair dice are rolled. Given that the total is 8, what is the probability that at least one dice shows a 6?
ms: Totals of 8: (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2). Two of these five contain a 6, so 2/5.
questions.tip: The condition restricts the sample space to the 5 outcomes with total 8.
steps: 'Given the total is 8' means only look at the ways to make 8.
Ones with a 6: (2,6) and (6,2). That is 2 ways.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue marbles. Two marbles are taken at random without replacement.
Given that both marbles are the same colour, work out the probability that they are both red.
questions.tip: The condition 'same colour' is your new total: P(RR) + P(BB).
steps: Same colour means both red or both blue. Work out each.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] For a grouped frequency table, what value do you use for each group when estimating the mean?
ms: Multiply each midpoint by its frequency, add, then divide by the total frequency.
questions.tip: The answer is an estimate because the exact values are unknown.
steps: In grouped data you do not know the exact values, so you pick one value to stand for each group.
The middle of the group is the fairest guess, so use the midpoint, multiply by frequency, add up, and divide by the total.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The table shows the times, t minutes, that 30 people waited at a bus stop.
Time (t minutes) | Frequency
0 < t ≤ 10 | 4
10 < t ≤ 20 | 10
20 < t ≤ 30 | 12
30 < t ≤ 40 | 4
Work out an estimate for the mean waiting time.
questions.tip: Divide by the total frequency (30), not by the number of groups (4).
steps: Use the midpoint of each group: 5, 15, 25, 35.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Using the same bus stop table (frequencies 4, 10, 12, 4 for 0-10, 10-20, 20-30, 30-40 minutes), which class contains the median?
ms: There are 30 values, so the median is about the 15.5th. Cumulative: 4, 14, 26, so it lies in 20 < t ≤ 30.
questions.tip: Use cumulative frequency to find which group holds the middle value.
steps: There are 30 values, so the median is halfway, around the 15th and 16th values.
14 is not enough to reach the 15th value, but 26 is, so the median is in the third group.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A table shows the number of pets owned: 0 pets: 3 people; 1 pet: 8 people; 2 pets: 6 people; 3 pets: 2 people; 4 pets: 1 person. What is the mean number of pets?
questions.tip: Divide by the total frequency (20), not by the number of rows (5). Averaging the values 0 to 4 gives 2, which is wrong.
steps: Mean = total pets ÷ number of people.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Class A has 12 students with a mean test score of 68. Class B has 18 students with a mean score of 73.
Work out the mean score of all 30 students.
questions.tip: Find the total scores first. Averaging 68 and 73 gives 70.5, which is wrong.
steps: You cannot average the two means, because the classes are different sizes. Find the total scores instead.
Class A total = 12 × 68 = 816. Class B total = 18 × 73 = 1314.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Five numbers have a mean of 8. A sixth number is added and the mean becomes 9.
Work out the sixth number.
questions.tip: Work with totals: mean × number of values.
steps: Work with totals. Five numbers with mean 8 have total 5 × 8 = 40.
Six numbers with mean 9 have total 6 × 9 = 54.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Explain why the mean calculated from a grouped frequency table is only an estimate, and state one reason why the median might be a better average to use if the data contains an extreme value.
questions.answer: The exact data values are not known, so midpoints are used. The median is not affected by extreme values (outliers), whereas the mean is.
ms: B1 for: the actual values are unknown / midpoints are used to represent each group
B1 for: the median is not affected by extreme values (outliers)
questions.tip: Use the key words 'midpoint' and 'outlier' or 'extreme value'.
steps: In a grouped table you only know which group each value is in, not the actual value.
So you use midpoints, which are guesses. That makes the mean an estimate.
An extreme value pulls the mean towards it, but the median is just the middle value, so it hardly changes.
Answer: The exact data values are not known, so midpoints are used. The median is not affected by extreme values (outliers), whereas the mean is.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the masses of some parcels.
Mass (m kg) | Frequency
0 < m ≤ 20 | 6
20 < m ≤ 40 | x
40 < m ≤ 60 | 4
An estimate of the mean mass is 28 kg.
Work out the value of x.
questions.tip: The total frequency is 10 + x, so it includes the unknown.
steps: Midpoints are 10, 30 and 50. Set up the mean as an equation with x.
Total frequency = 6 + x + 4 = 10 + x. So (260 + 30x) ÷ (10 + x) = 28.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] On a cumulative frequency graph with total frequency 80, at what cumulative frequency do you read off the lower quartile?
ms: Lower quartile is at 1/4 of the total: 80 ÷ 4 = 20.
questions.tip: Upper quartile is at 3/4 (60). Median is at 1/2 (40).
steps: The lower quartile is a quarter of the way through the data.
¼ of 80 = 80 ÷ 4 = 20, so read across from 20.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] When plotting a cumulative frequency graph for grouped data, where do you plot each point?
options: At the midpoint of each class
ms: Cumulative frequency is the running total up to the END of each class, so plot at the upper bound.
questions.tip: Plotting at midpoints is the most common error and loses the marks.
steps: Cumulative frequency is the running total up to the end of each class.
So the total only applies once the whole class is included: plot it at the upper class boundary.
Answer: At the upper class boundary

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A box plot has minimum 12, lower quartile 18, median 25, upper quartile 31, maximum 40. What is the interquartile range?
questions.tip: 28 is the range. IQR uses the quartiles.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two classes sat the same test.
Class P: median 54, IQR 12.
Class Q: median 61, IQR 25.
Compare the distributions of the scores for the two classes.
questions.answer: Class Q had a higher median, so on average Q scored higher. Class P had a smaller IQR, so P's scores were more consistent (less spread out).
ms: B1 for comparing medians in context, e.g. Class Q's scores were higher on average (median 61 > 54)
B1 for comparing IQRs in context, e.g. Class P's scores were more consistent as the IQR is smaller (12 < 25)
questions.tip: Compare one average and one measure of spread, both in context. Just stating the numbers does not score.
steps: A good comparison has two parts: one about the average (median) and one about spread (IQR), both in context.
Median: 61 > 54, so Class Q scored higher on average.
IQR: 12 < 25, so Class P's scores were more consistent.
Answer: Class Q had a higher median, so on average Q scored higher. Class P had a smaller IQR, so P's scores were more consistent (less spread out).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The cumulative frequency table shows the lengths of 80 phone calls.
Length (t minutes) | Cumulative frequency
t ≤ 10 | 8
t ≤ 20 | 26
t ≤ 30 | 52
t ≤ 40 | 70
t ≤ 50 | 80
(a) Which interval contains the median?
(b) Use the table to estimate how many calls lasted more than 40 minutes.
(c) Estimate how many calls lasted between 10 and 30 minutes.
ms: B1 for 20 < t ≤ 30 (40th value: cumulative frequency passes 40 there)
questions.tip: Subtract cumulative frequencies to get the number in a range.
steps: (a) The median is the 80 ÷ 2 = 40th value. Cumulative frequency is 26 at 20 min and 52 at 30 min, so it passes 40 between them.
