Drink A, ratio 1 : 4 (5 parts): 300 ÷ 5 = 60. Juice 60 ml, water 240 ml.
Drink B, ratio 2 : 3 (5 parts): 200 ÷ 5 = 40. Juice 80 ml, water 120 ml.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 3/4 of the money Ali has is equal to 2/3 of the money Bea has.
Work out the ratio of Ali's money to Bea's money. Give your answer in its simplest form.
questions.tip: Write an equation first. 3 : 4 or 2 : 3 are not the answer.
steps: Multiply both sides by 12 to clear fractions: 9A = 8B.
So A/B = 8/9, which means A : B = 8 : 9.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Concrete is made by mixing cement, sand and gravel in the ratio 1 : 2 : 4 by mass.
A builder needs 1.4 tonnes of concrete. 1 tonne = 1000 kg.
Cement is sold in 25 kg bags costing £5.85 each.
Sand costs £38 per tonne.
Gravel costs £32 per tonne.
Work out the total cost of the materials. The builder can only buy whole bags of cement.
questions.tip: Keep units consistent: sand and gravel are priced per TONNE, so use 0.4 t and 0.8 t.
steps: 1.4 tonnes = 1400 kg. Ratio 1 : 2 : 4 has 7 parts, so 1 part = 1400 ÷ 7 = 200 kg.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which of these tables shows y directly proportional to x?
ms: y ÷ x is always 5, so y = 5x
questions.tip: Direct proportion needs y ÷ x to be constant. 4, 6, 8 goes up evenly but 4 ÷ 1 ≠ 6 ÷ 2.
steps: Direct proportion means y ÷ x is always the same number.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 5 litres of paint cover 40 m².
How many litres of the same paint are needed to cover 72 m²?
questions.tip: Find what one unit does first (unitary method).
steps: Find what 1 litre covers: 40 ÷ 5 = 8 m² per litre.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The exchange rate is £1 = $1.25
(a) Change £240 into dollars. (1)
(b) Change $350 into pounds. (2)
questions.tip: Going from dollars to pounds you DIVIDE by the rate. Check: you should get fewer pounds than dollars.
steps: Check: there should be fewer pounds than dollars, and 280 < 350.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y is inversely proportional to x².
x is doubled.
What happens to y?
ms: y = k/x². Doubling x multiplies x² by 4, so y is divided by 4.
questions.tip: Square the scale factor and then take the reciprocal because it is inverse.
steps: y = k/x². If x doubles, x² becomes (2x)² = 4x².
The bottom of the fraction is 4 times bigger, so y is divided by 4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] t is inversely proportional to s.
Complete the table.
s | 2 | 5 | ?
t | 30 | ? | 4
questions.answer: When s = 5, t = 12; when t = 4, s = 15
questions.tip: For inverse proportion s × t is constant. Check: 5 × 12 = 60 and 15 × 4 = 60.
steps: Inverse proportion: s × t stays the same. k = 2 × 30 = 60.
Answer: When s = 5, t = 12; when t = 4, s = 15

questions.q:
[Calculator] A car uses 6.4 litres of fuel for every 100 km.
Fuel costs 148.9p per litre.
Work out the cost of the fuel for a journey of 365 km. Give your answer to the nearest penny.
questions.tip: Give money in pounds to 2 d.p. Leaving the answer as 3478.3 is wrong units.
steps: 365 km is 3.65 lots of 100 km, so fuel = 6.4 × 3.65 = 23.36 litres.
Change to pounds: 3478.3 ÷ 100 = £34.783, so £34.78 to the nearest penny.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y is directly proportional to the square of x.
When x = a, y = 18.
When x = a + 2, y = 50.
Given that a > 0, work out the value of a.
questions.tip: Divide the two equations to cancel k. Then square root both sides.
steps: y = kx². So 18 = ka² and 50 = k(a + 2)².
Divide the second by the first to cancel k: (a + 2)²/a² = 50/18 = 25/9.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] p is inversely proportional to the square of q.
When q = 4, p = 0.5
Work out the positive value of q for which p = q.
questions.tip: Find k first, then set p equal to q in your formula.
steps: So p = 8/q². Set p = q: q = 8/q².
Multiply by q²: q³ = 8, so q = 2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Pump A on its own empties a full tank in 9 hours.
Pump B on its own empties the same full tank in 6 hours.
Both pumps start emptying the full tank at the same time and work at their usual rates.
Work out how long it takes to empty the tank. Give your answer in hours and minutes.
ms: M1 rates 1/9 and 1/6 of the tank per hour (or in 18 hours A empties 2 tanks and B empties 3 tanks)
M1 1/9 + 1/6 = 5/18 of the tank per hour (or 5 tanks in 18 hours)
questions.tip: Add the RATES (fractions of the tank per hour), not the times. 9 + 6 = 15 or (9 + 6) ÷ 2 = 7.5 hours are wrong because two pumps must be quicker than either one alone.
steps: Add the rates, not the times. A empties 1/9 of the tank per hour, B empties 1/6.
Together: 1/9 + 1/6 = 2/18 + 3/18 = 5/18 of the tank per hour.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y is directly proportional to √x.
x is increased by 69%.
Show that y increases by 30%.
questions.answer: y = k√x; new x = 1.69x so new y = k√(1.69x) = 1.3k√x, a 30% increase
ms: M1 y = k√x and new x = 1.69x
A1 √1.69 = 1.3 so y is multiplied by 1.3, a 30% increase
questions.tip: Use the multiplier 1.69, then take the square root of the multiplier (13² = 169). Do not halve 69%.
steps: y = k√x. A 69% increase means x is multiplied by 1.69.
A multiplier of 1.3 is a 30% increase.
Answer: y = k√x; new x = 1.69x so new y = k√(1.69x) = 1.3k√x, a 30% increase

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A block has a mass of 600 g and a volume of 75 cm³.
What is its density?
questions.tip: Density is mass ÷ volume. 0.125 comes from dividing the wrong way round.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cyclist rides at an average speed of 18 km/h for 1 hour 40 minutes.
Work out the distance she travels.
questions.tip: 40 minutes is 2/3 of an hour, not 0.4 hours.
steps: 40 minutes = 40/60 = 2/3 of an hour, so the time is 1 2/3 = 5/3 hours.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cheetah can run at 30 m/s.
A car is travelling at 100 km/h.
Which is faster? You must show your working.
questions.answer: Cheetah: 30 m/s = 108 km/h, which is more than 100 km/h
ms: A1 the cheetah is faster, with correct comparison
questions.tip: Convert to the same units before comparing, and state which is faster.
steps: Change the cheetah's speed to km/h so you can compare.
108 000 m = 108 km, so 108 km/h. That is more than 100 km/h.
Answer: Cheetah: 30 m/s = 108 km/h, which is more than 100 km/h

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Water flows into a pond at 3 litres per second.
1 m³ = 1000 litres.
How many cubic metres of water flow into the pond in 10 minutes?
questions.tip: 10 minutes is 600 seconds. Then divide litres by 1000.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Kai runs 400 m in 80 seconds. He then runs a further 600 m in 170 seconds.
Work out his average speed for the whole 1000 m, in metres per second.
questions.tip: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Do not average the two speeds.
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A box has a weight of 120 N. It rests on a face measuring 40 cm by 30 cm.
(a) Work out the pressure on the floor in N/m². (3)
(b) The box is turned so it rests on a face measuring 30 cm by 20 cm. Work out the increase in pressure. (1)
ms: B1 new pressure 120 ÷ 0.06 = 2000 N/m², increase 1000 N/m²
questions.tip: Change cm to m BEFORE finding the area. 1200 cm² is 0.12 m², not 12 m².
steps: Pressure = force ÷ area, with area in m². 40 cm = 0.4 m and 30 cm = 0.3 m.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Liquid A has density 0.9 g/cm³. Liquid B has density 1.3 g/cm³.
400 cm³ of liquid A is mixed with V cm³ of liquid B.
The mixture has density 1.05 g/cm³.
Work out the value of V.
questions.tip: Densities do not add. Use total mass ÷ total volume.
steps: Densities don't add. Use mixture density = total mass ÷ total volume.
Mass of A = 400 × 0.9 = 360 g. Mass of B = 1.3V g.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A force acts on an area A and produces a pressure P.
The same force acts on an area that is 20% smaller.
Work out the percentage increase in the pressure.
questions.tip: Pressure is inversely proportional to area. 20% smaller area does not give 20% more pressure.
steps: Pressure = force ÷ area. A 20% smaller area means area × 0.8.
A multiplier of 1.25 is a 25% increase.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Town X and town Y are 300 km apart.
A train leaves X at 09:00 and travels towards Y at a constant 80 km/h.
A second train leaves Y at 09:30 and travels towards X at a constant 120 km/h.
At what time do the trains pass each other?
ms: M1 by 09:30 the first train has travelled 40 km, so 260 km apart
questions.tip: 1.3 hours is 1 hour 18 minutes, not 1 hour 30 minutes.
steps: By 09:30 the first train has gone 80 × 0.5 = 40 km, so they are 300 − 40 = 260 km apart.
They move towards each other, so the gap closes at 80 + 120 = 200 km/h.
Time to meet = 260 ÷ 200 = 1.3 hours = 1 hour 18 minutes (0.3 × 60 = 18).

questions.q:
[Calculator] Gold has a density of 19.3 g/cm³.
A gold bar is a cuboid measuring 18 cm by 5 cm by 3.5 cm.
Gold costs £62.40 per gram.
Work out the value of the gold bar.
questions.tip: Mass = density × volume. Do not divide.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A value is multiplied by 0.92 each year.
Which statement describes this?
ms: 0.92 = 1 − 0.08, so it decreases by 8% each year
questions.tip: A multiplier less than 1 means decrease. Subtract from 1 to get the percentage.
steps: 0.92 is less than 1, so the value goes down.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The population of a village is 3000. It increases by 10% each year.
Work out the population after 3 years.
questions.tip: Each year's 10% is of the NEW population. 3900 is simple growth, which is wrong.
steps: 10% growth each year means × 1.1 each year.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The value, £V, of a machine t years after it is bought is given by V = 4000 × 0.9^t
(a) Write down the value of the machine when it is bought. (1)
(b) Work out the value after 2 years. (1)
(c) Write down the percentage the value decreases by each year. (1)
questions.tip: When t = 0, 0.9⁰ = 1, so the starting value is the number in front.
steps: (a) When bought, t = 0 and 0.9⁰ = 1, so V = 4000.
(c) Multiplier 0.9 keeps 90%, so it loses 10% a year.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 640 g of a radioactive substance halves in mass every 3 days.
What mass is left after 12 days?
questions.tip: Count the halvings (12 ÷ 3 = 4). Do not divide 640 by 12.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A car is worth £12 000. Its value falls by 25% in the first year and by 20% in the second year.
Show that the car loses 40% of its value over the two years.
questions.answer: 0.75 × 0.8 = 0.6, so the car is worth 60% (£7200), a 40% loss
questions.tip: 25% + 20% = 45% is wrong. The 20% is of the reduced value.
steps: Overall multiplier 0.75 × 0.8 = 0.6, so it keeps 60% and loses 40%.
Answer: 0.75 × 0.8 = 0.6, so the car is worth 60% (£7200), a 40% loss

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A colony starts with 300 bacteria. The number doubles every 20 minutes.
How many bacteria are there after 2 hours?
questions.tip: Count how many 20-minute periods are in 2 hours (6), not 2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A price is decreased by x%. The new price is then increased by x%.
The final price is 4% lower than the original price.
Work out the value of x.
questions.tip: Use multipliers and expand: it is a difference of two squares.
steps: Use multipliers: (1 − x/100)(1 + x/100) = 0.96, because 4% lower is × 0.96.
This is a difference of two squares: 1 − x²/10 000 = 0.96.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] £P is invested for 2 years at 10% per year.
With compound interest it earns £21 more than it would with simple interest.
Work out the value of P.
questions.tip: Simple interest for 2 years at 10% is 20%; compound is 21%.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The population of bats in a cave was 2000 at the start of 2024 and 2662 at the start of 2027.
The population increased by the same percentage each year.
Work out (a) the percentage increase each year (2) and (b) the population at the start of 2025 (1).
questions.tip: 2024 to 2027 is THREE years, so 1.331 is a three-year multiplier. Take the cube root (11³ = 1331), not the square root, and do not divide 33.1% by 3.
steps: Yearly multiplier = ∛1.331 = 1.1, because 11³ = 1331. So (a) 10% a year.
(b) Start of 2025 is one year on: 2000 × 1.1 = 2200.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A boat loses 12% of its value each year.
(a) Show that after 5 years it has lost about 47% of its value. (2)
(b) After how many whole years will it first have lost more than 60% of its value? (2)
questions.tip: Losing more than 60% means the value is LESS than 40%, so compare with 0.4.
steps: Losing 12% a year means × 0.88 each year.
(b) Lost more than 60% means the value is below 40%, so below 0.4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A fair six-sided dice is rolled.
What is the probability that it lands on a prime number?
questions.tip: 1 is NOT a prime number. 2 is prime.
steps: Primes on a dice are 2, 3 and 5. (1 is not prime.)

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 4 red, 7 green and 9 white counters only. A counter is taken at random.
(a) Work out the probability that it is red. (1)
(b) Work out the probability that it is not green. (1)
questions.tip: Count the total first (20). 'Not green' = 1 − P(green).
steps: (b) Not green = red or white = 4 + 9 = 13, so 13/20.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Spinner A has three equal sections numbered 1, 2 and 3.
Spinner B has four equal sections numbered 1, 2, 3 and 4.
Both spinners are spun and the two scores are multiplied.
Work out the probability that the product is an even number.
ms: M1 a sample space of 12 outcomes (e.g. a grid of products)
questions.tip: A product is even if EITHER number is even. Use a grid so you do not miss any.
steps: There are 3 × 4 = 12 equally likely pairs. A product is even if either number is even.
B shows 2 or 4: always even, 3 × 2 = 6 outcomes.
B shows 1 or 3: even only when A shows 2, giving 2 more outcomes.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A spinner has three sections A, B and C.
P(A) = 2 × P(B) and P(C) = 3 × P(B).
What is P(B)?
questions.tip: All the probabilities must add to 1. Write them in terms of P(B).
steps: Write all in terms of P(B): P(A) = 2P(B), P(C) = 3P(B).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Kim spins a spinner 40 times. It lands on 5 eight times.
Ben spins the same spinner 160 times. It lands on 5 twenty times.
(a) Whose results give the better estimate of the probability of landing on 5? Give a reason. (1)
(b) Use all the results to work out the best estimate of the probability that the spinner lands on 5. (2)
questions.answer: (a) Ben, because he did more trials (b) 28/200 = 7/50 (0.14)
questions.tip: Combine the totals. Do not average the two relative frequencies (0.2 and 0.125).
steps: (a) More trials give a more reliable estimate. Ben did 160 spins, Kim only 40.
Answer: (a) Ben, because he did more trials (b) 28/200 = 7/50 (0.14)

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The probability that a battery is faulty is 0.04.
A shop sells 150 packs of batteries. Each pack contains 8 batteries.
Work out an estimate for the number of faulty batteries.
questions.tip: Find the total number of batteries first, not the number of packs.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains red, blue and yellow counters only.
The probability of taking a red counter is 0.4
The probability of taking a blue counter is twice the probability of taking a yellow counter.
There are 26 blue counters in the bag.
Work out the total number of counters in the bag.
questions.tip: Blue and yellow share 0.6 in the ratio 2 : 1.
steps: Red is 0.4, so blue and yellow share 1 − 0.4 = 0.6.
Blue is twice yellow, so split 0.6 in the ratio 2 : 1: blue 0.4, yellow 0.2.
0.4 of the counters are blue and that is 26 counters.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains x red counters and y blue counters only.
The probability of taking a red counter is 1/3.
4 more red counters are added to the bag. The probability of taking a red counter is now 1/2.
Work out the values of x and y.
questions.tip: Adding red counters changes BOTH the top and the bottom of the fraction.
steps: P(red) = 1/3 means red is 1 out of every 3, so blue is twice red: y = 2x.
After adding 4 red: (x + 4)/(x + y + 4) = 1/2. Put y = 2x: (x + 4)/(3x + 4) = 1/2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two fair four-sided dice are numbered 1, 2, 3 and 4. Both are rolled and the scores are added.
(a) Work out the probability that the total is a prime number. (2)
(b) The two dice are rolled 80 times. Work out an estimate for the number of times the total is a prime number. (1)
ms: M1 16 outcomes with totals 2, 3, 5 and 7 identified (1 + 2 + 4 + 2 = 9)
questions.tip: List all 16 outcomes. A total of 5 can happen 4 ways.
steps: There are 4 × 4 = 16 equally likely outcomes. Prime totals possible: 2, 3, 5, 7.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] P(A) = 0.7 and P(B) = 0.45
Explain why events A and B cannot be mutually exclusive.
questions.answer: If they were mutually exclusive, P(A or B) = 0.7 + 0.45 = 1.15, which is more than 1, which is impossible
ms: A1 states a probability cannot be greater than 1, so A and B must overlap
questions.tip: Mutually exclusive means they cannot both happen, so their probabilities just add.
steps: Mutually exclusive means A and B can't both happen, so P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B).
No probability can be more than 1, so A and B must overlap.
Answer: If they were mutually exclusive, P(A or B) = 0.7 + 0.45 = 1.15, which is more than 1, which is impossible

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A fair coin is flipped and a fair six-sided dice is rolled.
What is the probability of getting a head and a 6?
questions.tip: AND means multiply. Adding gives 2/3, which is wrong.
steps: The coin and dice don't affect each other, so multiply.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The probability that Ali wins a game is 0.3. He plays 2 games. The results are independent.
Work out the probability that he wins at least one of the games.
questions.tip: 'At least one' is quickest as 1 − P(loses both). 0.3 + 0.3 = 0.6 is wrong because it double counts winning both.
steps: 'At least one win' is everything except 'loses both'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 6 red and 4 yellow counters. A counter is taken at random, its colour is recorded and it is put back. A second counter is then taken.
Work out the probability that the two counters are different colours.
questions.tip: Different colours can happen two ways: red then yellow OR yellow then red.
steps: With replacement, the bag is the same each time: red 6/10, yellow 4/10.
Red then yellow: 6/10 × 4/10 = 24/100. Yellow then red: 4/10 × 6/10 = 24/100.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 2 red and 3 blue balls. Two balls are taken at random without replacement.
What is the probability that both are blue?
questions.tip: Without replacement the second fraction has one fewer blue AND one fewer in total.
steps: Without replacement: 2 blue left out of 4 balls, so 2/4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In each football match, the probability that a team wins is 0.5, draws is 0.2 and loses is 0.3.
A win scores 3 points, a draw 1 point and a loss 0 points.
The team plays two matches. The results are independent.
Work out the probability that the team scores at least 4 points.
ms: M1 identifies win-win (6 points) and win-draw in either order (4 points)
questions.tip: List the outcomes that give 4 or more points. Win-draw and draw-win are both needed.
steps: List results giving at least 4 points: win-win (6 points), win-draw or draw-win (4 points).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A box contains 10 chocolates. 7 are milk and 3 are dark. Lily takes two chocolates at random and eats them.
Work out the probability that at least one of the chocolates is dark.
questions.tip: 'At least one' is quickest as 1 − P(none).
steps: At least one dark = 1 − P(both milk).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 5 red counters and 3 green counters.
Jo takes a counter at random.
If it is red, she keeps it.
If it is green, she puts it back and also adds another green counter to the bag.
She then takes a second counter at random.
Work out the probability that the second counter is green.
questions.tip: The bag changes differently on each branch: after red there are 7 counters, after green there are 9.
steps: Two routes to a green second counter. The bag changes differently on each.
Red first (5/8): she keeps it, leaving 7 counters with 3 green. 5/8 × 3/7 = 15/56.
Green first (3/8): put back plus one more green, so 9 counters with 4 green. 3/8 × 4/9 = 12/72 = 1/6.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The probabilities that Sara passes her maths, English and science exams are 0.8, 0.7 and 0.6. The results are independent.
Work out the probability that she passes exactly two of the three exams.
questions.tip: Exactly two passed means exactly one failed. There are three ways.
steps: Exactly two passes means exactly one fail. Fail chances: 0.2, 0.3, 0.4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A biased spinner lands on red with probability x. It is spun twice.
The probability that it lands on red both times is 0.36.
Work out the probability that it lands on red exactly once.
questions.tip: Exactly once means red-not red OR not red-red: multiply by 2.
steps: Red both times: x × x = x² = 0.36, so x = 0.6. Not red = 0.4.
Exactly once: red then not, or not then red.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 2 red, 4 blue and 6 green counters. Two counters are taken at random without replacement.
Work out the probability that both counters are the same colour.
questions.tip: Same colour means both red OR both blue OR both green. Add the three products.
steps: Same colour means both red OR both blue OR both green. 12 counters in total.

questions.tip: A' means NOT in A. 1 is not prime, so it is in A'.
steps: Primes from 1 to 10: 2, 3, 5, 7. That is 4 numbers (1 is not prime).

questions.tip: ∩ means in both; ∪ means in either (or both). Do not list elements twice.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] There are 32 students in a class. 18 have a dog, 12 have a cat and 7 have both.
(a) Work out how many students have neither a dog nor a cat. (2)
(b) A student is chosen at random. Work out the probability that they have exactly one of these pets. (1)
ms: M1 dog only 11 and cat only 5
questions.tip: Put the 7 in the overlap first, then subtract to get the 'only' regions.
steps: Put 7 in the overlap. Dog only = 18 − 7 = 11. Cat only = 12 − 7 = 5.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which set describes the elements that are in neither A nor B?
ms: Not in A AND not in B is A' ∩ B', which is the same as (A ∪ B)'
questions.tip: A' ∪ B' includes everything except the overlap. That is not the same.
steps: In neither A nor B means NOT in A AND NOT in B.
Not in A is A', not in B is B', and 'and' is ∩.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] P(A) = 0.45, P(B) = 0.3 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.1
Work out
(a) P(A ∩ B') (1)
(b) P(A' ∩ B') (2)
questions.tip: Draw the Venn diagram with probabilities: A only = 0.35, B only = 0.2.
steps: Draw a Venn diagram with 0.1 in the overlap.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] There are 40 members in a club.
22 are in set A and 25 are in set B.
Work out (a) the least possible number and (b) the greatest possible number of members in A ∩ B.
ms: B1 (a) 7 (from 22 + 25 − 40, when nobody is in neither)
B1 (b) 22 (when all of A is inside B)
questions.tip: The overlap is smallest when everyone is in at least one set, and largest when the smaller set fits completely inside the bigger one.
steps: (a) The overlap is smallest when nobody is outside both sets.
Then 22 + 25 = 47 counts the overlap twice, so overlap = 47 − 40 = 7.
(b) The overlap is biggest when all of A (the smaller set) sits inside B: 22.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 100 people were asked which of France (F), Germany (G) and Italy (I) they have visited.
5 have visited all three.
12 have visited France and Germany.
15 have visited France and Italy.
10 have visited Germany and Italy.
40 have visited France, 35 have visited Germany and 38 have visited Italy.
(a) Work out how many people have visited none of the three countries. (3)
(b) A person is chosen at random. Work out the probability that they have visited exactly one of the countries. (1)
ms: M1 pairs only: 7 (F and G), 10 (F and I), 5 (G and I)
M1 only regions: F only 18, G only 18, I only 18
questions.tip: The 12 who visited France and Germany include the 5 who visited all three. Subtract the 5.
steps: Start in the middle with 5. Pairs only: F and G 12 − 5 = 7, F and I 15 − 5 = 10, G and I 10 − 5 = 5.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] For two events A and B:
P(A only) = 0.2, P(A ∩ B) = x, P(B only) = 2x, P(neither) = 0.35
(a) Work out the value of x. (2)
(b) Are A and B independent? You must show your working. (2)
questions.tip: For independence compare P(A) × P(B) with P(A ∩ B). They must be equal.
steps: All regions add to 1: 0.2 + x + 2x + 0.35 = 1, so 3x = 0.45.
Answer: (a) x = 0.15 (b) P(A) × P(B) = 0.35 × 0.45 = 0.1575 ≠ 0.15, so not independent

questions.tip: A ∩ B is multiples of 12 (the LCM), not multiples of 24.
steps: (c) Only look at B's 5 numbers. 2 are also in A: 2/5.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 80 people were asked if they like tea or coffee.
45 like tea and 50 like coffee.
The number who like both is twice the number who like neither.
Work out the number of people who like both.
questions.tip: Use one letter for the unknown and write every region in terms of it.
steps: All regions add to 80: (45 − 2n) + 2n + (50 − 2n) + n = 80, so 95 − n = 80.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the colour and type of 40 cars.
| Red | Blue
Saloon | 12 | 8
Hatchback | 15 | 5
A blue car is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is a saloon?
ms: There are 8 + 5 = 13 blue cars, 8 are saloons: 8/13
questions.tip: 'Given blue' means the denominator is the number of blue cars only.
steps: Given the car is blue, only look at blue cars: 8 + 5 = 13.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] There are 50 people in a room. 22 are men. 9 of the men wear glasses. 30 people in the room do not wear glasses.
(a) Work out how many women wear glasses. (1)
(b) A person who wears glasses is chosen at random. Work out the probability that this person is a woman. (1)
questions.tip: Draw a two-way table. 20 people wear glasses in total.
steps: (b) Given they wear glasses, choose from 20. 11 are women: 11/20.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] P(A) = 0.6
If A happens, the probability that B happens is 0.3
P(B) = 0.38
(a) If A does not happen, work out the probability that B happens. (2)
(b) Given that B happens, work out the probability that A happened. (2)
questions.tip: Draw the tree. P(A') = 0.4, and the B branch after A' must make the two B branches add to 0.38.
steps: Draw a tree. A and B: 0.6 × 0.3 = 0.18.
The two B branches add to 0.38, so not A and B = 0.38 − 0.18 = 0.2.
(a) P(not A) = 0.4, so the chance of B after not A = 0.2 ÷ 0.4 = 0.5.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Two fair coins are flipped. Given that at least one coin shows heads, what is the probability that both show heads?
ms: Outcomes with at least one head: HH, HT, TH. One of these is HH: 1/3
questions.tip: The condition removes TT, leaving 3 equally likely outcomes, not 4.
steps: Outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT. 'At least one head' removes TT.
That leaves 3 equally likely outcomes, and HH is 1 of them.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 200 people were tested for a virus. 40 of them have the virus.
The test was positive for 36 of the people who have the virus.
The test was also positive for 16 of the people who do not have the virus.
(a) Show this information on a frequency tree. (2)
(b) A person tests positive. Work out the probability that they have the virus. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 200 → 40 virus (36 positive, 4 negative), 160 no virus (16 positive, 144 negative) (b) 36/52 = 9/13
ms: B1 40 and 160 on the first branches
questions.tip: The denominator is ALL positive tests (36 + 16), not just the people with the virus.
steps: Virus: 36 positive, 40 − 36 = 4 negative. No virus: 16 positive, 160 − 16 = 144 negative.
Answer: (a) 200 → 40 virus (36 positive, 4 negative), 160 no virus (16 positive, 144 negative) (b) 36/52 = 9/13

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the options chosen by 90 students.
| Art | Music | Drama
Year 10 | 14 | 12 | 20
Year 11 | 18 | 10 | 16
(a) A student is chosen at random. Work out the probability that they chose music. (1)
(b) A Year 11 student is chosen at random. Work out the probability that they chose drama. (1)
(c) A student who chose art is chosen at random. Work out the probability that they are in Year 10. (1)
questions.tip: Each 'given' changes the denominator: total, Year 11 total, art total.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 5 red and 3 blue counters. Two counters are taken at random without replacement.
Given that the second counter is red, work out the probability that the first counter was red.
questions.tip: Find P(second red) using both branches. Do not assume it is 4/7 straight away.
steps: We are told the second is red, so divide by P(second red).
Red then red: 5/8 × 4/7 = 20/56. Blue then red: 3/8 × 5/7 = 15/56.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5 and P(A | B) = 0.3
(a) Work out P(A ∩ B). (1)
(b) Work out P(B | A). (2)
questions.tip: P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) ÷ P(B). Divide by the event you are GIVEN.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two fair six-sided dice are rolled.
Given that the product of the two scores is even, work out the probability that the sum of the two scores is also even.
ms: M1 27 outcomes have an even product (36 − 9 odd-odd)
M1 both even gives even product and even sum: 9 outcomes
questions.tip: An even product with an even sum needs BOTH dice even. Odd-odd gives an odd product.
steps: A product is odd only when both dice are odd: 3 × 3 = 9 outcomes. So even product: 36 − 9 = 27.
Even sum needs both odd or both even. Both odd gives an odd product, so only both even counts.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A factory has two machines. Machine A makes 60% of the items and machine B makes 40%.
3% of the items made by A are faulty. 4% of the items made by B are faulty.
An item is chosen at random and is faulty.
Work out the probability that it was made by machine A.
questions.tip: This is a 'reverse' conditional probability: divide the A-and-faulty branch by all faulty.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the shoe sizes of 20 students.
Shoe size | Frequency
5 | 3
6 | 7
7 | 6
8 | 4
What is the median shoe size?
ms: Median is halfway between the 10th and 11th values. Cumulative: 3, 10, 16, 20, so the 10th is 6 and the 11th is 7: median 6.5
questions.tip: The median is a shoe size, not a frequency. Use running totals to find the middle position.
steps: 20 values, so the median is halfway between the 10th and 11th.
Running totals: 3, 10, 16, 20. The 10th value is size 6, the 11th is size 7.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the times, t minutes, that 40 people waited for a train.
Time (t minutes) | Frequency
0 < t ≤ 5 | 14
5 < t ≤ 10 | 5
10 < t ≤ 15 | 6
15 < t ≤ 20 | 15
(a) Write down the modal class. (1)
(b) Write down the class that contains the median. (1)
questions.tip: The median is the 20.5th value. Running totals 14, 19, 25 put it in the third class.
steps: (a) The modal class has the highest frequency, 15: 15 < t ≤ 20.
(b) 40 values, so the median is the 20.5th. Running totals: 14, 19, 25.
The 20th and 21st are past 19 but within 25, so in the third class.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the masses, m kg, of 20 bags.
Mass (m kg) | Frequency
0 < m ≤ 4 | 3
4 < m ≤ 8 | 9
8 < m ≤ 12 | 6
12 < m ≤ 16 | 2
Work out an estimate for the mean mass.
questions.tip: Divide by the total frequency (20), not the number of classes (4).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Five whole numbers have a mean of 6, a median of 5, a mode of 4 and a range of 6.
Which could be the five numbers?
questions.tip: Check every condition. 4, 4, 5, 8, 9 has range 5; 4, 4, 5, 6, 10 adds to 29.
steps: Check each option for all four facts.
4, 4, 5, 7, 10: total 30, so mean 30 ÷ 5 = 6. Middle value 5. Mode 4. Range 10 − 4 = 6.
All four match. (4, 4, 5, 8, 9 has range 5; 4, 4, 5, 6, 10 adds to 29.)

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Here are five numbers.
3    7    9    12    x
x is greater than 9. The mean of the five numbers is equal to the median.
Work out the value of x.
questions.tip: With x bigger than 9, the numbers in order are 3, 7, 9, ... so the median is 9.
steps: x is bigger than 9, so in order the list is 3, 7, 9, then 12 and x. The median is 9.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The annual salaries of 6 people working in a small office are
£18 000    £19 000    £21 000    £22 000    £24 000    £96 000
(a) Work out the mean salary and the median salary. (2)
(b) Which average better represents the salaries? Give a reason. (1)
questions.answer: (a) mean £33 333 (to nearest £), median £21 500 (b) median, because the mean is affected by the extreme value of £96 000
ms: B1 median, with reason that £96 000 is an outlier that raises the mean above 5 of the 6 salaries
questions.tip: Say WHY: the mean is pulled up by one extreme value.
steps: Median: middle two are 21 000 and 22 000, so (21 000 + 22 000) ÷ 2 = 21 500.
(b) The £96 000 pulls the mean above 5 of the 6 salaries, so the median is more typical.
Answer: (a) mean £33 333 (to nearest £), median £21 500 (b) median, because the mean is affected by the extreme value of £96 000

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the number of goals a team scored in each of 20 matches.
Goals | Frequency
0 | 4
1 | 7
2 | 5
3 | 3
4 | 1
(a) Work out the mean number of goals per match. (2)
(b) The team plays some more matches and scores exactly 4 goals in each of them. The mean for all the matches is now 2.
Work out how many more matches the team played. (2)
questions.tip: Work with TOTALS: total goals and total matches both increase.
steps: (b) n more matches add 4n goals: (30 + 4n) ÷ (20 + n) = 2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the times, t minutes, 40 students took to complete a puzzle.
Time (t minutes) | Frequency
0 < t ≤ 10 | 5
10 < t ≤ 15 | 10

20 < t ≤ 40 | 10
Work out an estimate for the mean time. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: Unequal class widths do not change the method, but check each midpoint carefully (the last is 30).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A set of numbers has a mean of 8 and a range of 5.
Each number is multiplied by 3 and then 2 is added.
Work out the mean and the range of the new set of numbers.
questions.tip: Adding 2 to every number moves the data but does not change the spread.
steps: Multiplying every number by 3 multiplies the mean by 3, and adding 2 adds 2 to the mean.
The range is a gap, so the × 3 stretches it but the + 2 does not change it: 3 × 5 = 15.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The table shows the weekly pay, £p, of 60 workers.
Pay (£p) | Frequency
200 < p ≤ 300 | 12
300 < p ≤ 400 | 23
400 < p ≤ 600 | 18
600 < p ≤ 1000 | 7
(a) Work out an estimate for the mean weekly pay. (3)
(b) Estimate the number of workers who earn more than £500 a week. (1)
questions.tip: In (b), £500 is halfway through the 400 to 600 class, so take half of 18.
steps: (b) £500 is halfway through 400 to 600, so about half of 18 = 9 earn over £500 there. Plus all 7 above £600.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Here are 7 numbers in order.
3    5    6    8    9    11    14
What is the lower quartile?
questions.tip: Put data in order first. For n values the LQ is the (n + 1)/4 th value.
steps: The data is already in order. For n values, the lower quartile is the (n + 1)/4 th value.
(7 + 1) ÷ 4 = 2, so the LQ is the 2nd value.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the masses, m kg, of 40 parcels.
Mass (m kg) | Frequency
0 < m ≤ 10 | 5
10 < m ≤ 20 | 12
20 < m ≤ 30 | 18
30 < m ≤ 40 | 5
(a) Complete a cumulative frequency table for this data. (1)
(b) How many parcels have a mass of 20 kg or less? (1)
questions.tip: Cumulative frequency is a running total. The last value must equal the total, 40.
steps: (b) '20 kg or less' is the running total at the end of the 10 to 20 class: 17.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Here are the ages of 15 people in order.
12  15  17  18  20  21  23  24  26  27  29  30  33  35  41
Work out (a) the median (1), (b) the interquartile range (2).
ms: M1 LQ = 18 (4th value) and UQ = 30 (12th value)
questions.tip: For 15 values the quartiles are the 4th and 12th values.
steps: 15 values, so the median is the (15 + 1) ÷ 2 = 8th value: 24.
LQ is the (15 + 1) ÷ 4 = 4th value: 18. UQ is the 3 × 4 = 12th value: 30.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cumulative frequency graph for the times of 60 people is drawn by joining these points with straight lines:
(0, 0), (10, 6), (20, 21), (30, 45), (40, 57), (50, 60)
Estimate the median time.
ms: Median at cumulative frequency 30: between (20, 21) and (30, 45). 20 + (9/24) × 10 = 23.75
questions.tip: Read across at 30 (half of 60), then down to the time axis.
steps: 60 people, so read the median at cumulative frequency 30.
30 is between (20, 21) and (30, 45). It is 30 − 21 = 9 of the 24 steps up that line.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A box plot shows the test scores of 80 students.
Minimum 20, lower quartile 38, median 52, upper quartile 61, maximum 85.
(a) Estimate how many students scored more than 61. (1)
(b) Estimate how many students scored between 38 and 52. (1)
(c) Jamal says, 'Half the students scored between 38 and 61.' Is he correct? Give a reason. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 20 (b) 20 (c) Yes, the IQR contains the middle 50% of the data
ms: B1 yes, the values between the quartiles are the middle 50%
questions.tip: Each section of a box plot holds about 25% of the data, whatever its width.
steps: Each section of a box plot holds about a quarter of the data. A quarter of 80 = 20.
(a) Above the UQ (61) is the top quarter: 20.
(b) Between LQ and median is one quarter: 20.
(c) Between the quartiles is the middle half, so he is right.
Answer: (a) 20 (b) 20 (c) Yes, the IQR contains the middle 50% of the data

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The cumulative frequency table shows the heights, h cm, of 100 plants.
Height (h cm) | Cumulative frequency
h ≤ 10 | 5
h ≤ 20 | 25
h ≤ 30 | 65
h ≤ 40 | 85
h ≤ 50 | 100
A cumulative frequency graph is drawn by joining the points (0, 0), (10, 5), (20, 25), (30, 65), (40, 85) and (50, 100) with straight lines.
Use the graph to estimate the interquartile range.
questions.tip: For n = 100 read at 25 and 75 on the cumulative frequency axis.
steps: 100 plants, so read the quartiles at cumulative frequency 25 and 75.
cf 25 is exactly at the point (20, 25), so LQ = 20.
cf 75 is halfway between (30, 65) and (40, 85), so UQ = 35.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cumulative frequency graph for the times, in minutes, of 120 runners is drawn by joining these points with straight lines:
(20, 0), (25, 12), (30, 42), (35, 84), (40, 108), (45, 120)
Estimate the percentage of runners who took more than 37 minutes.
questions.tip: The graph gives the number AT OR BELOW a value. Subtract from the total for 'more than'.
steps: Read the cumulative frequency at 37 minutes. 37 is 2/5 of the way from 35 to 40.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cumulative frequency graph for the scores of 80 boys is drawn by joining these points with straight lines:
(0, 0), (10, 4), (20, 20), (30, 60), (40, 72), (50, 80)
For the girls, the median score was 31 and the interquartile range was 14.
Compare the scores of the boys and the girls.
questions.answer: Boys: median 25, IQR 10. Girls scored higher on average (31 > 25); boys' scores were more consistent (IQR 10 < 14)
ms: M1 boys' median 25 read from the graph
M1 boys' LQ 20 and UQ 30, IQR 10
A1 girls had a higher median so did better on average
A1 boys had a smaller IQR so their scores were more consistent
questions.tip: Make one comparison of average and one of spread, and say what each means in context.
steps: 80 boys: median at cf 40, quartiles at cf 20 and 60.
cf 40 is halfway between (20, 20) and (30, 60): median 25. cf 20 gives LQ 20, cf 60 gives UQ 30.
Average: girls' median 31 > boys' 25, so girls scored higher on average.
Spread: boys' IQR 10 < girls' 14, so boys' scores were more consistent.
Answer: Boys: median 25, IQR 10. Girls scored higher on average (31 > 25); boys' scores were more consistent (IQR 10 < 14)

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The cumulative frequency table gives the times, t minutes, of 40 phone calls.
Time (t minutes) | Cumulative frequency
t ≤ 10 | 6
t ≤ 20 | 20
t ≤ 30 | 34
t ≤ 40 | 40
All times are greater than 0.
Work out an estimate for the mean length of a call.
questions.tip: You cannot use the cumulative frequencies in fx. Change them back into frequencies first.
steps: Turn the cumulative frequencies back into frequencies: 6, 20 − 6 = 14, 34 − 20 = 14, 40 − 34 = 6.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cumulative frequency graph for the exam marks of 160 students is drawn by joining these points with straight lines:
(0, 0), (20, 8), (40, 40), (60, 104), (80, 148), (100, 160)
The pass mark is set so that 70% of the students pass.
Estimate the pass mark.
questions.tip: The students who fail are at the bottom of the graph, so read at 30%, not 70%.
steps: 70% pass, so the bottom 30% fail. 30% of 160 = 48 students.
Read the mark at cf 48: between (40, 40) and (60, 104). That is 8 of the 64 steps up.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the frequencies for some grouped data.
0 < x ≤ 10: 20
10 < x ≤ 15: 15
15 < x ≤ 30: 30
30 < x ≤ 50: 20
On a histogram, which class has the tallest bar?
ms: Frequency densities: 2, 3, 2, 1. The tallest bar is 10 < x ≤ 15
questions.tip: The tallest bar has the greatest frequency DENSITY, not the greatest frequency.
steps: Bar height is frequency density = frequency ÷ width.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Work out the frequency density for each class.
Time (t s) | Frequency
0 < t ≤ 20 | 16
20 < t ≤ 30 | 24
30 < t ≤ 35 | 15
35 < t ≤ 50 | 9
ms: M1 frequency ÷ class width for at least one class
questions.tip: Class width is the difference between the boundaries (35 − 30 = 5), not the upper value.
steps: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width. Widths: 20, 10, 5, 15.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A histogram has these bars.
0 < x ≤ 5: frequency density 4
5 < x ≤ 10: frequency density 6
10 < x ≤ 20: frequency density 3.5
20 < x ≤ 40: frequency density 1
Work out the total frequency.
ms: M1 frequency = fd × width for at least two bars (20, 30, 35, 20)
questions.tip: Frequency is the AREA of each bar: density × width.
steps: Frequency = density × width for each bar.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In a histogram, the bar for 15 < x ≤ 25 represents 32 people.
The bar for 25 < x ≤ 30 is the same height.
How many people does the bar for 25 < x ≤ 30 represent?
ms: Same height, half the width, so half the area: 16
questions.tip: Same height does not mean same frequency when the widths differ.
steps: Frequency is the area of the bar. Same height, so compare widths.
15 to 25 is 10 wide. 25 to 30 is 5 wide, which is half.
Half the width means half the frequency: 32 ÷ 2 = 16.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A histogram has these bars.
0 < x ≤ 10: frequency density 1.2
10 < x ≤ 20: frequency density 2.8
20 < x ≤ 25: frequency density 6
25 < x ≤ 40: frequency density 2
Estimate the number of values between 15 and 30.
questions.tip: For part of a class, use the part of the width you need (5), not the whole width.
steps: Use density × the part of the width you need.
20 to 25 (whole bar): 5 × 6 = 30. 25 to 30 (5 of the 25 to 40 bar): 5 × 2 = 10.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Complete the table.
Height (h cm) | Frequency | Frequency density
0 < h ≤ 10 | 15 | 1.5
10 < h ≤ 15 | ? | 5.2
15 < h ≤ 30 | 36 | ?
questions.tip: Frequency = fd × width (5 × 5.2); fd = frequency ÷ width (36 ÷ 15).
steps: Frequency = density × width. 10 to 15 has width 5: 5.2 × 5 = 26.
Density = frequency ÷ width. 15 to 30 has width 15: 36 ÷ 15 = 2.4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A histogram has these bars.

Work out an estimate for the mean.
questions.tip: Turn the densities back into frequencies before using midpoints.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The times, t minutes, of 100 people are shown in a histogram.
0 < t ≤ 10: frequency density 2
10 < t ≤ 15: frequency density 4.8
15 < t ≤ 25: frequency density not shown
25 < t ≤ 40: frequency density 1.2
(a) Work out the frequency density for 15 < t ≤ 25. (3)
(b) One of the people is chosen at random. Work out the probability that their time was more than 25 minutes. (1)
questions.tip: Use the total frequency: the missing class must make the frequencies add to 100.
steps: They add to 62, so the missing class has 100 − 62 = 38.
(b) More than 25 minutes is the last class: 18 people, so 18/100 = 9/50.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In a histogram, the bar for 20 < x ≤ 30 is twice as tall as the bar for 30 < x ≤ 60.
Liam says, 'There are more values in 20 < x ≤ 30 than in 30 < x ≤ 60.'
Is Liam correct? Explain your answer.
questions.answer: No. If the shorter bar has height h, the frequencies are 10 × 2h = 20h and 30 × h = 30h, so 30 < x ≤ 60 has more
ms: M1 compares areas: 10 × 2h and 30 × h (or equivalent)
A1 Liam is wrong, 30 < x ≤ 60 has more values
questions.tip: Compare AREAS, not heights.
steps: In a histogram, frequency = area = height × width.
Let the 30 to 60 bar have height h. Its frequency = 30 × h = 30h.
The 20 to 30 bar has height 2h and width 10: 10 × 2h = 20h.
30h > 20h, so 30 < x ≤ 60 has more values. Liam is wrong.
Answer: No. If the shorter bar has height h, the frequencies are 10 × 2h = 20h and 30 × h = 30h, so 30 < x ≤ 60 has more

questions.q:
[Calculator] The table shows the lengths, L cm, of 79 fish.
Length (L cm) | Frequency
0 < L ≤ 5 | 12
5 < L ≤ 12 | 21
12 < L ≤ 20 | 28
20 < L ≤ 35 | 18
(a) Work out the frequency density for each class. (1)
(b) Estimate the number of fish longer than 16 cm. (2)
questions.tip: 16 is halfway through the 12 to 20 class, so take half its frequency, then add the whole of the next class.
steps: (b) 16 to 20 is 4 of the 8 cm in that class: 4 × 3.5 = 14 fish.
Then add all 18 fish in 20 to 35: 14 + 18 = 32.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A head teacher asks 50 of the 900 students in her school about school lunches.
What is the population?
ms: The population is the whole group being studied: all 900 students
questions.tip: The 50 students are the SAMPLE. The population is everyone the survey is about.
steps: The population is the whole group the survey is about. The 50 asked are the sample.
The survey is about the school's students.
Answer: All 900 students in the school

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A gym has 600 members. Describe how to take a simple random sample of 40 members.
questions.answer: Number the members 1 to 600, use a random number generator to pick 40 different numbers, and select those members
ms: B1 give each member a number (or a list of all members)
B1 use a random number generator (or names drawn from a hat) to choose 40, ignoring repeats
questions.tip: 'Pick them randomly' is not enough. Say how each member gets an equal chance.
steps: Every member must have an equal chance of being picked.
Get a list of all 600 members and number them 1 to 600.
Use a random number generator to pick 40 different numbers, ignoring any repeats.
Answer: Number the members 1 to 600, use a random number generator to pick 40 different numbers, and select those members

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A stratified sample by gender of 45 students is taken from a school.
The sample contains 20 girls.
There are 360 boys in the school.
Work out the number of students in the school.
questions.tip: Each sampled boy represents the same fraction of the school as each sampled girl.
steps: Stratified means the sample keeps the same fractions, so boys are 25/45 of the school.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Capture-recapture is used to estimate the number of fish in a lake.
Which of these would make the estimate unreliable?
options: Some of the marks fall off the fish between the two samples
The marked fish are released back into the lake before the second sample
The second sample is the same size as the first
The fish are caught with the same type of net both times
ms: If marks fall off, fewer marked fish are recaptured, so the estimate is too high. The method assumes the marks stay on and the population does not change.
questions.tip: Releasing the marked fish so they mix back in is part of the method, not a problem.
steps: The method assumes the marked fish keep their marks.
If marks fall off, fewer fish look marked in the second catch, which makes the estimate too high.
Answer: Some of the marks fall off the fish between the two samples

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] There are 240 students in Year 11: 132 boys and 108 girls.
Lucy wants to find the mean time Year 11 students spend on homework.
(a) She first asks 10 students. Give one reason why this sample may not be reliable. (1)
(b) She then takes a stratified sample of 60 students by gender. Work out the number of boys and the number of girls in her sample. (2)
questions.answer: (a) The sample is too small (b) 33 boys and 27 girls
ms: B1 sample too small to represent 240 students (or not stratified/random)
questions.tip: Check that your two numbers add to the sample size, 60.
steps: (a) 10 out of 240 is too few to represent the whole year.
Answer: (a) The sample is too small (b) 33 boys and 27 girls

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A council wants to find out how residents travel to work.
It telephones 200 numbers from a landline phone book between 10 am and 2 pm on weekdays.
(a) Give two reasons why this sample is likely to be biased. (2)
(b) Suggest one way to improve the sampling method. (1)
questions.answer: (a) People at work in the day will not answer, so commuters are left out; people without landlines are left out (b) e.g. choose a random sample from the electoral register and survey at different times
ms: B1 calls during working hours miss people who are at work
B1 people without a landline are excluded
B1 a suitable improvement, e.g. random sample from a full list of residents, contact at different times or by different methods
questions.tip: Bias reasons must be specific to the context. 'It is not random' alone scores nothing.
steps: (a) Calling 10 am to 2 pm on weekdays misses people who are at work, which is exactly who the survey is about.
Using a landline phone book leaves out people with only mobiles.
(b) Pick randomly from a full list of residents and contact people at different times.

Answer: (a) People at work in the day will not answer, so commuters are left out; people without landlines are left out (b) e.g. choose a random sample from the electoral register and survey at different times

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] On Monday, 30 birds in a wood are caught, ringed and released.
On Tuesday, 50 birds are caught. 10 of them are ringed.
On Wednesday, 40 birds are caught. 6 of them are ringed.
(a) Work out an estimate of the number of birds using Tuesday's sample and using Wednesday's sample. (2)
(b) Which of the two estimates is likely to be more reliable? Give a reason. (1)
(c) Give a reason why the two estimates are different. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 150 and 200 (b) Tuesday's, because more birds were caught in that sample (c) e.g. samples are random so vary, or birds may have moved into or out of the wood
ms: B1 Tuesday's estimate, because the sample is larger (50 birds, with more ringed birds recaptured)
B1 a valid reason: natural variation between random samples, or the population changing
questions.tip: Use N = (number marked × second sample size) ÷ number marked in the sample.
steps: Use N = marked × catch size ÷ marked in catch.
(b) Tuesday's sample was bigger (50 birds, 10 ringed), so it is more reliable.
(c) Random samples vary, and birds may have flown in or out between days.
Answer: (a) 150 and 200 (b) Tuesday's, because more birds were caught in that sample (c) e.g. samples are random so vary, or birds may have moved into or out of the wood

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A school has 1200 students.
Year 10 boys: 300
Year 10 girls: 240
Year 11 boys: 360
Year 11 girls: 300
A stratified sample by year group and gender is taken. The sample contains 18 Year 10 girls.
Work out the number of Year 11 boys in the sample.
questions.tip: The fraction sampled is the same for every group: 18 out of 240.
steps: Every group is sampled at the same rate. Year 10 girls: 18 out of 240 = 3/40.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 120 birds on an island are caught, ringed and released.
A week later, 90 birds are caught and 18 of them are ringed.
(a) Estimate the number of birds on the island. (2)
(b) Ringed birds are easier to catch than birds without rings. Will your estimate be too high or too low? Explain why. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 600 (b) Too low: there will be too many ringed birds in the second sample, making the estimate smaller than the true population
ms: B1 too low, because a higher proportion of ringed birds in the sample makes the estimate smaller
questions.tip: More marked animals in the second sample means you divide by a bigger number, so the estimate falls.
steps: (b) If ringed birds are easier to catch, too many ringed birds appear in the second sample.
Dividing by a bigger number makes the estimate smaller, so it is too low.
Answer: (a) 600 (b) Too low: there will be too many ringed birds in the second sample, making the estimate smaller than the true population

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two random samples are taken from the same population to estimate the mean number of hours of screen time people have each evening.
Sample A: 20 people, mean 4.2 hours.
Sample B: 80 people, mean 3.8 hours.
(a) Which sample is likely to give the more reliable estimate? Give a reason. (1)
(b) Use both samples to work out the best estimate of the population mean. (2)
questions.answer: (a) Sample B, it is larger (b) 3.88 hours
ms: B1 sample B because it is larger
questions.tip: Weight each mean by its sample size. (4.2 + 3.8) ÷ 2 = 4 is wrong.
steps: (a) Bigger samples are more reliable, so Sample B (80 people).
Total = 84 + 304 = 388 hours for 100 people, so mean = 388 ÷ 100 = 3.88.
Answer: (a) Sample B, it is larger (b) 3.88 hours

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] These points are plotted on a scatter graph.
(1, 9), (2, 7), (3, 6), (4, 4), (5, 2)
What type of correlation is shown?
ms: As x increases, y decreases: negative correlation
questions.tip: Negative correlation means one goes up while the other goes down.
steps: y goes down as x goes up.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the hours spent revising and the test scores of 6 students.
Hours | 2 | 4 | 5 | 7 | 8 | 10
Score | 35 | 48 | 52 | 66 | 70 | 81
(a) Describe the correlation. (1)
(b) Another student revised for 6 hours and scored 20. What name is given to a point like this? (1)
questions.tip: Write 'positive correlation', not just 'it goes up'.
steps: (a) More hours of revision go with higher scores.
(b) A point far away from the pattern of the rest is called an outlier.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows five pairs of values.
x | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10
y | 15 | 19 | 26 | 29 | 36
A line of best fit should pass through the mean point.
Show that the mean point is (6, 25).
questions.answer: Mean of x = 30/5 = 6, mean of y = 125/5 = 25
questions.tip: Use the mean point to help you draw a good line of best fit.
steps: Answer: Mean of x = 30/5 = 6, mean of y = 125/5 = 25

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The line of best fit for a scatter graph of temperature, x °C, and the number of hot drinks sold, y, has equation y = 120 − 8x.
Estimate the number of hot drinks sold when the temperature is 9 °C.
questions.tip: Multiply before subtracting. (120 − 8) × 9 is the wrong order.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A line of best fit on a scatter graph of temperature (x °C) against the number of cold drinks sold (y) passes through the points (12, 21) and (27, 57).
(a) Work out the gradient of the line. (2)
(b) Interpret the gradient in this context. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 2.4 (b) about 2.4 more cold drinks are sold for each 1 °C rise in temperature
ms: B1 for each extra 1 °C, about 2.4 more drinks are sold
questions.tip: Interpreting a gradient means 'for each extra 1 unit of x, y changes by...'.
steps: (a) Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (57 − 21) ÷ (27 − 12) = 36 ÷ 15 = 2.4.
(b) Gradient means change in y for each 1 unit of x.
Answer: (a) 2.4 (b) about 2.4 more cold drinks are sold for each 1 °C rise in temperature

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A scatter graph shows the heights and weights of 8 dogs. The points are widely spread but show a slight upward trend.
Tom uses a line of best fit to estimate the weight of a dog from its height.
Give two reasons why his estimate may not be reliable.
questions.answer: The correlation is weak; the sample of 8 dogs is small
ms: B1 the correlation is weak (points widely spread)
B1 the sample is small (only 8 dogs)
questions.tip: Reasons must refer to the data given: strength of correlation and sample size.
steps: Points widely spread with only a slight trend means the correlation is weak.
Only 8 dogs is a small sample.
Answer: The correlation is weak; the sample of 8 dogs is small

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A scatter graph shows the outside temperature, x °C, and the amount of heating oil, y litres, a school uses each day.
The line of best fit passes through (5, 62) and (25, 22).
The data on the graph have x values from 5 to 25.
(a) Find the equation of the line of best fit in the form y = mx + c. (2)
(b) Use your equation to estimate the temperature on a day when the school uses 50 litres of oil. (1)
(c) Interpret the gradient of the line in this context. (1)
questions.answer: (a) y = −2x + 72 (b) 11 °C (c) for each 1 °C rise in temperature, the school uses about 2 litres less oil per day
ms: B1 about 2 litres less oil per day for each extra 1 °C (must mention both variables)
questions.tip: A falling line has a negative gradient. When interpreting it, say 'for each 1 °C increase, y decreases by about 2 litres'.
steps: (c) Gradient −2: for each 1 °C warmer, about 2 litres less oil.
Answer: (a) y = −2x + 72 (b) 11 °C (c) for each 1 °C rise in temperature, the school uses about 2 litres less oil per day

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the ages and values of 7 cars of the same model.
Age (years) | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7
Value (£1000s) | 18 | 16 | 14.5 | 13 | 20 | 10 | 8.5
(a) Identify the outlier. (1)
(b) Suggest a reason for the outlier. (1)
(c) Ignoring the outlier, estimate the value of a car that is 4.5 years old. (1)
questions.answer: (a) (5, 20) (b) e.g. it has very low mileage or is in excellent condition (c) about £12 000 (accept £11 500 to £12 500)
ms: B1 a sensible reason, e.g. low mileage, rare extras, excellent condition
B1 value in the range £11 500 to £12 500
questions.tip: Ignore the outlier when you draw or use the line of best fit.
steps: (a) Values mostly fall each year, but the 5-year-old car is worth £20 000, more than the 1-year-old. That is the outlier.
(b) It may have very low mileage or be in excellent condition.
(c) Ignoring it, 4 years is £13 000 and values fall roughly £1500 a year.
Half a year on from 4 years: about 13 000 − 750 ≈ £12 000.
Answer: (a) (5, 20) (b) e.g. it has very low mileage or is in excellent condition (c) about £12 000 (accept £11 500 to £12 500)

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The line of best fit on a scatter graph passes through the mean point (6, 25) and has gradient 2.5.
(a) Find the equation of the line of best fit. (2)
(b) Use it to estimate y when x = 9. (1)
questions.tip: Substitute the mean point to find c.
steps: (a) The line is y = 2.5x + c. Put in the mean point (6, 25): 25 = 2.5 × 6 + c.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the number of weeks, x, since a plant was planted and its height, y cm.
x | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8
y | 5 | 12 | 17 | 20 | 22 | 23 | 23.5 | 24
(a) Describe the relationship between x and y. (1)
(b) Explain why a straight line of best fit is not suitable for this data. (1)
questions.answer: (a) As x increases y increases, but the rate of growth slows down and levels off (b) the points follow a curve, not a straight line
ms: B1 positive relationship that levels off / increases at a decreasing rate
B1 the relationship is non-linear (a curve), so a straight line would not fit well
questions.tip: Correlation describes the trend, but always check whether the trend is actually a straight line.
steps: Look at how much y goes up each week: +7, +5, +3, +2, +1, +0.5, +0.5.
(a) y keeps rising, but by less each week, so it levels off.
(b) Because the jumps shrink, the points bend into a curve, so a straight line won't fit.
Answer: (a) As x increases y increases, but the rate of growth slows down and levels off (b) the points follow a curve, not a straight line

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Expand and simplify (x + 5)(x - 3)
questions.tip: Watch the sign of the constant: (+5) × (-3) = -15, and the x terms are -3x + 5x = +2x.
steps: Multiply every term in the first bracket by every term in the second (FOIL).
Collect the x terms: -3x + 5x = 2x. So the result is x² + 2x - 15.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise x² + 3x - 28
ms: M1 for (x ± 7)(x ± 4) or two numbers with product -28 and sum 3
questions.tip: Check by expanding: the pair must multiply to -28 AND add to +3, so the bigger number is positive.
steps: Find two numbers that multiply to -28 and add to +3.
Try factor pairs of 28: 7 × -4 = -28 and 7 + -4 = 3. These work.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise fully 8x²y - 12xy³
ms: The HCF of 8x²y and 12xy³ is 4xy, leaving 2x - 3y² inside the bracket.
questions.tip: 'Fully' means take out the highest common factor. If the bracket still has a common factor (like 4x - 6y²), it is not finished.
steps: Fully means take out the highest common factor (HCF) of everything.
Numbers: HCF of 8 and 12 is 4. Letters: both have at least one x and one y, so xy. HCF = 4xy.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Expand and simplify (x + 4)(x - 1)(2x + 3)
ms: M1 for expanding two brackets correctly, e.g. x² + 3x - 4
M1 for multiplying their quadratic by the third bracket with at least 4 of the 6 terms correct
questions.tip: Expand two brackets first and simplify before multiplying by the third. Most lost marks are sign slips in the middle terms.
steps: Do two brackets first, then multiply by the third.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise 3x² - 14x + 8
ms: M1 for (3x ± 2)(x ± 4) or for splitting the middle term: 3x² - 12x - 2x + 8
questions.tip: Both signs must be negative because the constant is + and the x term is -. Expand to check you get -14x, not -10x.
steps: Multiply the first and last numbers: 3 × 8 = 24. Find two numbers that multiply to 24 and add to -14: -12 and -2.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise fully 2x³ - 32x
ms: M1 for taking out a common factor, e.g. 2x(x² - 16)
questions.tip: After taking out 2x, spot the difference of two squares. Stopping at 2x(x² - 16) loses the accuracy mark.
steps: Take out the common factor first: 2x³ - 32x = 2x(x² - 16).
x² - 16 is a difference of two squares: x² - 4² = (x + 4)(x - 4).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Show that (x + 3)(2x - 1)² can be written in the form ax³ + bx² + cx + d, where a, b, c and d are integers.
ms: M1 for multiplying by (x + 3) with at least 4 of the 6 terms correct
questions.tip: (2x - 1)² is NOT 4x² + 1. Write it as (2x - 1)(2x - 1) and expand properly.
steps: Square the bracket properly, it is not just 4x² + 1: (2x - 1)² = (2x - 1)(2x - 1) = 4x² - 4x + 1.
Collect: 4x³ + 8x² - 11x + 3, so a = 4, b = 8, c = -11, d = 3.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise fully 4x² - (x - 3)²
ms: M1 for recognising a difference of two squares: (2x - (x - 3))(2x + (x - 3)) or for expanding to 3x² + 6x - 9
questions.tip: Use brackets when you subtract (x - 3): 2x - (x - 3) = x + 3, not x - 3. Then take out the common factor 3 for 'fully'.
steps: Spot a difference of two squares: A² - B² = (A - B)(A + B), with A = 2x and B = (x - 3).
(2x - (x - 3))(2x + (x - 3)) = (x + 3)(3x - 3). Careful with the minus sign in the first bracket.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Given that (2x + a)(x - 5) ≡ 2x² + bx - 15, find the value of a and the value of b.
questions.tip: Compare coefficients one at a time: the constants give a first, then use a to find b. Don't forget the -10x term.
steps: ≡ means both sides are identical for every x, so expand and match terms.
Match the x terms: b = -10 + a = -10 + 3 = -7.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise 6x² - 7xy - 20y²
questions.tip: With two variables, factorise exactly as with one: the outer and inner products must add to -7xy. Swapping signs gives +7xy.
steps: Quickest way with options: expand each one and see which gives -7xy in the middle.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Simplify fully (x² + 4x)/(x² - 16)
questions.tip: Factorise top and bottom first. You can only cancel whole brackets, never individual terms like x² with x².
steps: Factorise top and bottom so you can cancel brackets (never cancel single terms).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write (x + 1)/3 + (x - 2)/4 as a single fraction in its simplest form.
ms: M1 for a common denominator of 12 with at least one numerator correct, e.g. (4(x + 1) + 3(x - 2))/12
questions.tip: Multiply the WHOLE numerator by the factor: 3(x - 2) = 3x - 6, not 3x - 2.
steps: Use a common denominator: LCM of 3 and 4 is 12.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Simplify fully (3x² - 12)/(x² + x - 6)
ms: M1 for factorising the numerator: 3(x² - 4) or 3(x + 2)(x - 2)
questions.tip: Take out the common factor 3 first, then spot the difference of two squares. Cancel the (x - 2) bracket only.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 2/(x - 3) + 5/(x + 1) as a single fraction in its simplest form.
questions.tip: 5(x - 3) = 5x - 15, so the constant is 2 - 15 = -13. Leaving the bracket unexpanded loses the final mark.
steps: Common denominator: multiply the two denominators, (x - 3)(x + 1).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Simplify fully (x² - 25)/(2x + 10) × 6/(x - 5)
questions.tip: Factorise everything before multiplying. Multiplying out first makes cancelling almost impossible.
steps: Cancel (x + 5) top and bottom, and (x - 5) top and bottom.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 1/(x - 3) + 6/(x + 1) = 1
ms: M1 for reducing to a 3-term quadratic: x² - 9x + 14 = 0
M1 for correct factorisation (x - 2)(x - 7) = 0 or correct use of the formula
questions.tip: Multiply EVERY term by the common denominator, including the 1 on the right. Forgetting to multiply the 1 is the classic error.
steps: Clear the fractions by multiplying every term by (x - 3)(x + 1).
Move everything to one side: x² - 9x + 14 = 0.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 2x/(x + 3) - 1/(x - 1) = 1
questions.tip: When you reach x² - 5x = 0, factorise to x(x - 5) = 0. Dividing by x throws away the solution x = 0.
steps: Multiply every term by (x + 3)(x - 1) to clear the fractions.
Factorise: x(x - 5) = 0. Do not divide by x, or you lose the x = 0 solution.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve 1/(x - 2) + 2/(x + 1) = 1
Give your answers in the form a ± √b, where a and b are integers.
ms: M1 for correct substitution into the formula, x = (4 ± √12)/2, or completing the square (x - 2)² = 3
questions.tip: Simplify √12 = 2√3 and then divide BOTH terms of 4 ± 2√3 by 2. Leaving (4 ± √12)/2 is not in the required form.
steps: Rearrange: x² - 4x + 1 = 0. It does not factorise, so complete the square.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Show that (x² - 3x)/(x² - 9) ÷ 2x/(x + 3) simplifies to 1/2
ms: M1 for turning the division into multiplication by the reciprocal (x + 3)/(2x)
A1 for cancelling fully to 1/2 with all steps shown
questions.tip: Flip the SECOND fraction only, then cancel. In a 'show that' every factorising step must be written down.
steps: Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by it flipped: ÷ 2x/(x + 3) becomes × (x + 3)/(2x).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 3/(x + 2) - (x - 7)/(x² + x - 2) as a single fraction in its simplest form.
questions.tip: Subtracting (x - 7) changes BOTH signs: -x + 7. Then look for a common factor in the numerator so you can cancel.
steps: Factorise the second denominator: x² + x - 2 = (x + 2)(x - 1). So the common denominator is (x + 2)(x - 1).
Numerator: 3(x - 1) - (x - 7) = 3x - 3 - x + 7 = 2x + 4. Watch the minus sign on the -7.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve x² - 5x - 24 = 0
questions.tip: Once factorised, change the sign: (x - 8) = 0 gives x = +8.
steps: Factorise: find two numbers that multiply to -24 and add to -5: -8 and 3.
Each bracket can be zero: x - 8 = 0 gives x = 8, x + 3 = 0 gives x = -3.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve x² = 6x
ms: A1 for both x = 0 and x = 6
questions.tip: Do not divide both sides by x: you lose the solution x = 0. Rearrange to = 0 and factorise.
steps: Do not divide by x, as that loses a solution. Move everything to one side: x² - 6x = 0.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve x² - 4x - 1 = 0
Give your solutions in the form a ± √b, where a and b are integers.
ms: M1 for correct substitution into the formula: (4 ± √(16 + 4))/2, or for (x - 2)² - 5 = 0
questions.tip: -4ac with a = 1, c = -1 is +4, so the discriminant is 16 + 4 = 20, not 12.
steps: It does not factorise, so complete the square: x² - 4x = (x - 2)² - 4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (a) Write x² - 10x + 31 in the form (x - a)² + b. (2)
(b) Hence write down the minimum value of x² - 10x + 31. (1)
ms: B1 for minimum value 6 (ft their b)
questions.tip: Subtract the square of half the coefficient: 31 - 25 = 6. The minimum value is b, not a.
steps: (a) Halve the x coefficient: -10 ÷ 2 = -5, so start with (x - 5)².
(b) A square is never negative, so the smallest (x - 5)² can be is 0 (when x = 5). Minimum = 0 + 6 = 6.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 3x² + 10x - 8 = 0
ms: M1 for (3x ± 2)(x ± 4) or correct substitution into the formula
questions.tip: From (3x - 2) = 0, x = 2/3, not 2 or 3/2. Solve each bracket properly.
steps: Multiply first and last: 3 × -8 = -24. Two numbers multiplying to -24 and adding to 10: 12 and -2.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which expression gives the solutions of 2x² + 3x - 4 = 0?
questions.tip: The denominator is 2a = 4, and -4ac = -4(2)(-4) = +32. Square b before anything else.
steps: Quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) ÷ 2a. Here a = 2, b = 3, c = -4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (a) Write 2x² + 12x + 7 in the form a(x + b)² + c. (2)
(b) Hence solve 2x² + 12x + 7 = 0, giving your answers in surd form. (2)
questions.tip: Take out the 2 from the x² and x terms only. Then -9 inside the bracket becomes -18 outside: -18 + 7 = -11.
steps: (a) Take out the 2 from the x terms: 2(x² + 6x) + 7.
Complete the square inside: x² + 6x = (x + 3)² - 9. So 2[(x + 3)² - 9] + 7 = 2(x + 3)² - 18 + 7 = 2(x + 3)² - 11.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve 3x² - 2x - 2 = 0
Give your answers in the form (a ± √b)/c, where a, b and c are integers.
questions.tip: Simplify √28 to 2√7 then cancel the common factor 2 from every term. -4ac = -4(3)(-2) = +24.
steps: Use the formula with a = 3, b = -2, c = -2.
Divide top and bottom by 2: x = (1 ± √7)/3.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A right-angled triangle has sides of length x cm and (x + 7) cm, and hypotenuse (x + 8) cm.
Work out the area of the triangle.
ms: A1 for x = 5 (rejecting x = -3 because a length cannot be negative)
questions.tip: (x + 7)² is x² + 14x + 49. Give a reason for rejecting the negative root.
steps: x = 5 (x = -3 is impossible as a length). Sides are 5 and 5 + 7 = 12, hypotenuse 13.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 2(x + 3)² = 5(x + 3) + 3
ms: M1 for a substitution such as u = x + 3 giving 2u² - 5u - 3 = 0, or for expanding to 2x² + 7x = 0
questions.tip: If you substitute u = x + 3, remember to convert back to x at the end. u = 3 is not the answer.
steps: (x + 3) appears twice, so let u = x + 3: 2u² = 5u + 3, so 2u² - 5u - 3 = 0.
Swap back: x + 3 = 3 gives x = 0. x + 3 = -1/2 gives x = -1/2 - 3 = -7/2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
x + y = 10
x - y = 4
ms: Adding gives 2x = 14, so x = 7 and y = 3.
questions.tip: Always substitute back into BOTH equations to check: 7 + 3 = 10 and 7 - 3 = 4.
steps: The y terms are +y and -y, so adding the equations gets rid of y.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
4x + 3y = 5
2x - y = 5
ms: M1 for a correct method to eliminate one variable, e.g. multiplying the second equation by 3 and adding, or y = 2x - 5 substituted
questions.tip: When you multiply an equation to match coefficients, multiply EVERY term, including the number on the right.
steps: Make the y terms match: multiply the second equation by 3: 6x - 3y = 15.
Add to the first: (4x + 3y) + (6x - 3y) = 5 + 15, so 10x = 20 and x = 2.
Substitute into 2x - y = 5: 4 - y = 5, so y = -1.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
3x - 4y = 18
5x + 3y = 1
ms: M1 for multiplying to get equal coefficients, e.g. 9x - 12y = 54 and 20x + 12y = 4
M1 for correctly adding or subtracting to eliminate one variable: 29x = 58
questions.tip: Same signs subtract, different signs add. Here the y terms are -12y and +12y, so ADD.
steps: Make the y coefficients equal: × 3 the first gives 9x - 12y = 54, × 4 the second gives 20x + 12y = 4.
The signs are different, so add: 29x = 58, so x = 2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 4 coffees and 3 muffins cost £13.70
2 coffees and 5 muffins cost £12.80
Work out the cost of one coffee and the cost of one muffin.
ms: M1 for forming both equations: 4c + 3m = 13.70 and 2c + 5m = 12.80 (or in pence)
M1 for a correct elimination, e.g. doubling the second: 4c + 10m = 25.60, then 7m = 11.90
questions.tip: Working in pence (1370 and 1280) avoids decimal slips. Give money answers with 2 decimal places and a £ sign.
steps: Let c = cost of a coffee and m = cost of a muffin: 4c + 3m = 13.70 and 2c + 5m = 12.80.
Double the second to match the c terms: 4c + 10m = 25.60.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which gives all the solutions of the simultaneous equations y = x² - 2 and y = x + 4?
questions.tip: Find y by substituting into the LINEAR equation; it is quicker and less error-prone. Pair each x with its own y.
steps: Both equal y, so set them equal: x² - 2 = x + 4.
Rearrange: x² - x - 6 = 0, so (x - 3)(x + 2) = 0, giving x = 3 or x = -2.
Find y from y = x + 4: x = 3 gives y = 7, x = -2 gives y = 2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
y = 2x² - 3x
y = x + 6
questions.tip: Rearrange to = 0 before factorising. Each x value needs its matching y value for full marks.
steps: Both equal y, so set them equal: 2x² - 3x = x + 6.
Use y = x + 6: x = 3 gives y = 9, x = -1 gives y = 5.
Answer: x = 3, y = 9 or x = -1, y = 5

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
x² + y² = 10
x + 2y = 5
ms: M1 for rearranging the linear equation: x = 5 - 2y
questions.tip: (5 - 2y)² = 25 - 20y + 4y². Write out both brackets: squaring term by term (25 + 4y²) is wrong.
steps: Rearrange the linear one: x = 5 - 2y. Substitute into the circle.
y = 1 gives x = 5 - 2 = 3. y = 3 gives x = 5 - 6 = -1.
Answer: x = 3, y = 1 or x = -1, y = 3

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
x² + xy = 12
x - y = 2
ms: M1 for y = x - 2 substituted: x² + x(x - 2) = 12
questions.tip: x(x - 2) = x² - 2x. Divide the quadratic through by 2 to make factorising easier.
steps: Rearrange the linear one: y = x - 2. Substitute into the other.
x² + x(x - 2) = 12, so 2x² - 2x - 12 = 0. Divide by 2: x² - x - 6 = 0.
y = x - 2: x = 3 gives y = 1, x = -2 gives y = -4.
Answer: x = 3, y = 1 or x = -2, y = -4

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The line y = x + 1 meets the curve y = x² - 3x + 2 at the points A and B.
Find the exact coordinates of A and B.
ms: M1 for correct use of the formula or completing the square: (x - 2)² = 3
questions.tip: 'Exact' means leave answers as surds. y = x + 1, so add 1 to each x value, keeping the matching sign.
steps: At the meeting points the y values are equal: x² - 3x + 2 = x + 1.
Rearrange: x² - 4x + 1 = 0. Complete the square: (x - 2)² - 4 + 1 = 0, so (x - 2)² = 3.
y = x + 1, so y = 3 + √3 when x = 2 + √3, and y = 3 - √3 when x = 2 - √3.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A rectangle has a perimeter of 34 cm and a diagonal of length 13 cm.
Use algebra to find the length and width of the rectangle.
ms: M1 for x² + (17 - x)² = 169 leading to x² - 17x + 60 = 0
questions.tip: Perimeter 34 means length + width = 17, not 34. 'Use algebra' means a trial-and-improvement answer scores nothing.
steps: Let length = x and width = y. Perimeter: 2x + 2y = 34, so x + y = 17.
The diagonal makes a right-angled triangle: x² + y² = 13² = 169.
Substitute y = 17 - x: x² + (17 - x)² = 169, so 2x² - 34x + 289 = 169, giving x² - 17x + 60 = 0.
Factorise: (x - 12)(x - 5) = 0, so x = 12 or x = 5. The other side is 17 - x.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 3(x - 2) ≥ 9
questions.tip: Expand the bracket fully: 3 × (-2) = -6. Writing 3x - 2 gives 11/3.
steps: Treat it like an equation. Expand: 3x - 6 ≥ 9.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] -5 < 2x + 1 ≤ 9
x is an integer. Write down all the possible values of x.
questions.tip: < means the end value is NOT included, so -3 is not allowed, but ≤ means 4 is.
steps: Do the same thing to all three parts. Subtract 1: -6 < 2x ≤ 8.
-3 is not included (strict <), 4 is included (≤). Integers: -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve (5 - 2x)/3 > x - 5
ms: M1 for multiplying both sides by 3: 5 - 2x > 3x - 15
questions.tip: Multiply the WHOLE right side by 3: 3(x - 5) = 3x - 15. If you divide by a negative, flip the sign.
steps: Multiply both sides by 3 to clear the fraction: 5 - 2x > 3x - 15.
Divide by 5: 4 > x, which is the same as x < 4.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve x² + 3x - 10 ≤ 0
ms: M1 for critical values found: (x + 5)(x - 2), giving -5 and 2
M1 for identifying the region between the roots (e.g. a sketch)
questions.tip: Sketch the U-shaped curve. ≤ 0 means the part BELOW the x-axis, which is between the roots.
steps: Solve the equals version first to find the critical values: (x + 5)(x - 2) = 0, so x = -5 or x = 2.
Sketch y = x² + 3x - 10: a U-shape crossing the x-axis at -5 and 2.
≤ 0 means where the curve is on or below the axis, which is between the roots.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which gives the solution of 2x² > 18 in set notation?
ms: x² > 9 means x is more than 3 away from 0: x < -3 or x > 3.
questions.tip: Square-rooting an inequality gives TWO regions. Writing x > ±3 is not accepted.
steps: Divide by 2: x² > 9. Critical values are x = 3 and x = -3.
y = x² - 9 is a U-shape, above the axis outside the roots. So x < -3 or x > 3 (e.g. x = 0 fails, x = 4 works).
In set notation, 'or' is written with ∪.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A region R is a triangle bounded by the three lines x = 1, y = x and x + y = 8. All boundary lines are solid and the point (2, 4) lies inside R.
Write down the three inequalities that define R.
questions.tip: Test a point inside the region in each line to find the direction. Solid lines mean ≤ or ≥, dashed mean < or >.
steps: For each line, use the point (2, 4) to decide which side is inside. Lines are solid, so use ≥ or ≤.
x = 1: at (2, 4), x = 2, which is bigger than 1, so x ≥ 1.
y = x: at (2, 4), y = 4 is more than x = 2, so y ≥ x.
x + y = 8: at (2, 4), 2 + 4 = 6, which is less than 8, so x + y ≤ 8.
Answer: x ≥ 1, y ≥ x, x + y ≤ 8

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve 2x² - 5x - 12 > 0
Give your answer in set notation.
ms: M1 for (2x + 3)(x - 4) or critical values -3/2 and 4
M1 for identifying the regions outside the roots
B1 for correct set notation {x : x < -3/2} ∪ {x : x > 4}
questions.tip: > 0 means ABOVE the x-axis: the two outside regions. Don't join them as -3/2 > x > 4, which is impossible.
steps: Find critical values: 2x² - 5x - 12 = (2x + 3)(x - 4) = 0, so x = -3/2 or x = 4.
The graph is a U-shape. > 0 means above the axis, which is outside the roots.
